items.title: [Bug]: Matrix auto_thread / session_scope=thread isolates sessions correctly but replies still post at room level (no m.thread relation)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Bug Description

If the human starts a real Matrix thread (reply-in-thread to their own message), the bot replies in-thread correctly and sustains it — real thread roots are honored end-to-end.
But *synthetic* (auto-created) roots fail to materialize as wire-level threads.

## Possibly related
- #20243 — Discord auto-thread failure silently falls back to inline channel reply
- #26058 — auto_thread skipped for free_response_channels
Same failure *shape* on sibling adapters: auto-thread intent silently degrading to inline.

### Steps to Reproduce

## Repro
1. Matrix room (E2EE or not), `require_mention: true`, `auto_thread: true`,
   `session_scope: thread` (or unset). Restart gateway.
2. Send a top-level `@bot` message in the room.
3. Bot replies as a rich reply in the main timeline; no thread is created.
4. Control: reply-in-thread to your own message and @mention — bot threads correctly.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), upstream `83016547`
- Docker deployment (shipped compose), Matrix platform via matrix-nio, E2EE room
- Single human operator + bot in a normal (non-DM) room; `require_mention: true`

## Config
```yaml
matrix:
  require_mention: true
  session_scope: thread   # also reproduced with session_scope absent (auto) + auto_thread: true
  auto_thread: true
```
Confirmed the YAML→env bridge applies these (`MATRIX_SESSION_SCOPE=thread`,
`MATRIX_AUTO_THREAD=true`), gateway restarted after every change.

### Expected Behavior

## Expected (per docs, `user-guide/messaging/matrix.md`)
- "**Auto-threading** — By default, Hermes auto-creates a thread for each message it responds to in a room."
- `session_scope: thread` — "Unthreaded room messages synthesize a thread/session from the triggering event ID."
- "Matrix uses **threaded**, editable thinking/tool-activity panes…"

## Ask
Propagate the synthetic thread root into reply/pane metadata so `auto_thread` /
`session_scope: thread` produce real MSC3440 threads as documented — or, if
session-only scoping is the intent, update the docs to say auto-threading affects
session bookkeeping but not wire-level threads.

### Actual Behavior

- Replies to top-level room messages arrive as plain room messages carrying only a rich reply (`m.relates_to.m.in_reply_to`) — **no `rel_type: m.thread`** — so no thread is created in any threading-capable client (verified in Element).
- Thinking/tool-activity panes likewise post to the main timeline, not a thread.
- **Session isolation itself works**: with `session_scope: thread`, consecutive top-level messages demonstrably get separate contexts (previously, under `session_scope: room`, a stale unanswered request merged into a later reply — switching scope fixed that half). So the *synthetic thread root exists internally*; it just never reaches the wire.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug bundle uploaded to Nous (private):
  View URL  https://support.nousresearch.com/diagnostics/b6541482-e5c9-4413-bb8c-aecc2fafc517
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 26.04

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), upstream `83016547`

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

## Source-level trace (v0.18.0 line numbers)
1. Inbound: `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py` `_resolve_message_context` cascade
   (~L2674–2687) correctly sets `thread_id = event_id` for the synthetic root (both via
   `session_scope == "thread"` and via the `_auto_thread` fallback), marks it in
   `ThreadParticipationTracker`, and passes it into `build_source(..., thread_id=…)`.
2. Outbound: `_apply_relation_metadata` (~L3999) attaches
   `rel_type: m.thread` + `is_falling_back` **iff `metadata["thread_id"]` is present** —
   the mechanism exists and works (that's how real-root replies thread).
3. Observed replies lack the thread relation ⇒ the interactive reply path does not
   propagate the synthetic `source.thread_id` back into the outbound `metadata` dict.
   (`gateway/delivery.py` has `send_metadata["thread_id"]` handling on some paths; the
   live room-reply path appears not to populate it for synthetic roots.)

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Caveat up front: this is from static reading of v0.18.0 — I'm not set up to
runtime-validate a patch right now — but the trace narrows the defect well.

Every component I could trace handles the synthetic root correctly in isolation:

- inbound: matrix adapter `_resolve_message_context` sets the synthetic
  `thread_id` and passes it into `build_source(..., thread_id=...)` (~L2674-2687)
- outbound: `_apply_relation_metadata` (~L3999) attaches `rel_type: m.thread`
  whenever `metadata["thread_id"]` is present (this is why real-root replies work)
- `gateway/delivery.py` copies `target.thread_id` into `send_metadata` (~L525)
- `gateway/run.py:_thread_metadata_for_source` builds `{"thread_id": ...}`
  correctly, and several send sites already use it (e.g. the queued-turn notice
  at ~run.py:5061-5079, the notice path at ~run.py:8513)

So the drop appears to be that the *interactive turn's* initial reply/progress
post does not attach thread metadata. Note Matrix streams responses by editing
(`m.replace`, adapter ~L1736), so the INITIAL post's metadata alone decides
whether the whole reply threads — one missed call site is sufficient to explain
the symptom.

Suggested fix shape: at the interactive turn's initial reply/pane send site(s),
build metadata via the existing `_thread_metadata_for_source(event.source, ...)`
helper, exactly as the queued-turn notice path already does — rather than
omitting metadata. (An alternative — having the matrix adapter fall back to its
own `ThreadParticipationTracker` when metadata lacks `thread_id` — would also
work but risks threading unrelated sends; the explicit-metadata route matches
the sibling call sites.)

Quick confirmation for whoever picks this up: a one-line debug log of `metadata`
inside `_apply_relation_metadata` will show which call site posts the visible
reply without `thread_id` on the first repro turn.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Update dialog close button (×) unresponsive when opened by clicking version in bottom-right corner (macOS)
items.body:
## Bug Description

In the Hermes Desktop app on macOS, when the **New update available** dialog is opened by clicking on the client version string in the bottom-right corner of the window, the close button (×) in the top-right corner of the dialog is unresponsive. Clicking it does nothing — the dialog stays open. The only way to dismiss it is to click the **Maybe later** link at the bottom.

**Note:** This is related to but distinct from #66611 (which is about the "Already up to date" overlay). This bug occurs with the **"New update available"** dialog (with "Update now" + "Maybe later" buttons), on **macOS**.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the Hermes Desktop app on macOS
2. Click the version string in the bottom-right corner (or wait for an update check to find a new version)
3. Wait for the update dialog to appear — shows "New update available", release notes, "Update now" button, and "Maybe later" link
4. Click the **× (close button)** in the top-right corner of the dialog
5. **Result:** Nothing happens — the dialog does not close
6. Click **Maybe later** — **Result:** Dialog closes successfully

## Expected Behavior

- Clicking the × button should close/dismiss the update dialog (same as "Maybe later")
- Pressing **Esc** should also close the dialog

## Actual Behavior

- × button click does nothing — no visual feedback, no dialog close
- "Maybe later" link works as expected

## Related

- #66611 — similar issue but for the "Already up to date" overlay (not the "New update available" dialog)

## Affected Component

Desktop app (`apps/desktop/**`).

## Operating System

- **OS:** macOS
- **Platform:** Hermes Desktop native app

items.title: Custom/Ollama provider: effort: none produces MORE reasoning than effort: low (wrong code path in build_api_kwargs_extras)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
Summary

For custom/Ollama providers, setting reasoning_config.effort: "none" produces worse reasoning suppression than setting effort: "low" — the opposite of the intended behavior. This is caused by a hardcoded special case in CustomProfile.build_api_kwargs_extras() that routes effort == "none" through extra_body.think = False, a field that Ollama's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint silently ignores. Every other non-empty effort value takes a different code path that emits a top-level reasoning_effort field, which Ollama does honor.

Environment

  • Hermes Agent: v0.18.2 (build 2026.7.7.2), install method: docker

  • Provider: custom (self-hosted Ollama, local network, OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions, api_mode: chat_completions)

  • Ollama version: 0.24.0

  • Model: locally built Qwen3-8B GGUF import (Q5_K_M), hybrid-thinking capable (Qwen3 ChatML template with IsThinkSet/Think support)

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Configure a custom_providers entry pointing at a local Ollama instance serving a hybrid-thinking Qwen3 model.

  2. Set:

    reasoning_config:
      enabled: true
      effort: none

  3. Send a trivial prompt (e.g. "Say only OK.") through this provider.

  4. Compare against the same prompt with effort: low instead.

Expected Behavior

effort: none should suppress reasoning at least as effectively as effort: low, since "none" is semantically the strongest suppression request.

Actual Behavior

effort: none produces full reasoning (measured: 134 completion tokens, ~15–18s latency on an 8-core CPU VPS), because it is special-cased to emit extra_body.think = False, which Ollama's /v1/chat/completions endpoint silently drops (confirmed independently — see verification below).

effort: low produces partial reasoning suppression (measured: 73 completion tokens, ~11s), because a non-"none" effort value takes the elif branch and emits a top-level reasoning_effort field instead, which Ollama's endpoint does honor.

Directly querying Ollama with a top-level reasoning_effort: "none" field (bypassing Hermes entirely) produces 3 completion tokens and near-instant response — proving the underlying mechanism works correctly, and that the special case in Hermes' custom-provider plugin is actively preventing the optimal, intended behavior.

Root Cause

plugins/model-providers/custom/__init__.py, build_api_kwargs_extras():

if reasoning_config and isinstance(reasoning_config, dict):
    _effort = (reasoning_config.get("effort") or "").strip().lower()
    _enabled = reasoning_config.get("enabled", True)
    if _effort == "none" or _enabled is False:
        extra_body["think"] = False
    elif _effort:
        top_level["reasoning_effort"] = _effort

The comment above this block (# Ollama-only flag and thinking is already server-default-on for these backends, so forcing it risks a 400 on GLM/vLLM endpoints that don't recognize it) suggests extra_body.think was chosen deliberately to avoid breaking non-Ollama custom endpoints (GLM-5.2/ARK, vLLM). That reasoning may hold for those backends, but it actively breaks the intended "none" behavior specifically for Ollama, which is one of the primary backends this provider type targets (per the module docstring: "Ollama instances and OpenAI-compatible reasoning endpoints").

Verification Data

All three requests below were sent with an identical prompt ("Sag nur OK.") against the same locally built Qwen3-8B model, isolating Hermes/Ollama interaction from model behavior:

Suggested Fix

Emit the top-level reasoning_effort field for effort == "none" as well, instead of (or in addition to) extra_body.think:

if reasoning_config and isinstance(reasoning_config, dict):
    _effort = (reasoning_config.get("effort") or "").strip().lower()
    _enabled = reasoning_config.get("enabled", True)
    if _enabled is False:
        extra_body["think"] = False
    if _effort == "none":
        top_level["reasoning_effort"] = "none"
    elif _effort:
        top_level["reasoning_effort"] = _effort

If the concern noted in the original comment (breaking GLM/vLLM endpoints that don't recognize a bare reasoning_effort: "none") is still valid, consider making the target field configurable per-provider-instance, or detecting Ollama specifically (e.g. via a base_url heuristic or an explicit backend: ollama flag) rather than hardcoding one field for all custom endpoints. Happy to test a patch against our local Ollama instance if useful.

Impact

For CPU-only local Ollama deployments (no GPU), the difference between the current behavior and the fix is the difference between a usable low-latency dispatcher and a multi-second-per-request bottleneck that defeats the purpose of using a small local model at all.

items.title: [Bug]: run_tests.sh cannot run tests touching Path.home() on native Windows — env -i strips USERPROFILE

labels.name: sweeper:risk-automation
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect CI, automerge, label sync, or maintainer automation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

`scripts/run_tests.sh` builds its hermetic environment with `env -i` passing only `PATH, HOME, TZ, LANG, LC_ALL, PYTHONHASHSEED`. CPython on Windows ignores `HOME`: `Path.home()` / `expanduser` resolve via `USERPROFILE` (or `HOMEDRIVE`+`HOMEPATH`), which `env -i` strips. Result: on native Windows (Git Bash — the environment the PowerShell installer itself sets up), every test file that touches `Path.home()` dies at collection:

```
RuntimeError: Could not determine home directory.
```

This takes out the entire `tests/gateway/` directory (e.g. `test_42039_duplicate_user_message.py`: 0 collected, 1 error) and any other suite importing modules that resolve a home directory. The same hermetic env also drops `SYSTEMROOT` (needed by `ssl`/sockets on Windows) and `TEMP`/`TMP` (tempfile).

Separately, the runner and its per-file subprocesses print `✓`/`⚠` glyphs; Windows consoles default to a legacy codepage, so output crashes with:

```
UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u2713' ... (cp1252)
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Native Windows 11, Git Bash, repo venv per CONTRIBUTING
2. `HERMES_PYTHON=.venv/Scripts/python.exe bash scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_42039_duplicate_user_message.py`
3. Collection error above; with flaky output, the UnicodeEncodeError too

### Expected Behavior
The canonical runner works on native Windows — the README advertises native Windows as fully supported, and CONTRIBUTING says to use `scripts/run_tests.sh` before every PR.

### Root Cause
`env -i` allowlist is POSIX-centric: `HOME` is passed but Windows Python never reads it (`ntpath.expanduser`). None of the missing vars (`USERPROFILE`, `HOMEDRIVE`, `HOMEPATH`, `SYSTEMROOT`, `TEMP`, `TMP`) carry secrets, so passing them through preserves the hermetic intent (credential stripping).

### Environment
Windows 11 (native), Python 3.11.15, Git Bash (MinGit), current main (`14add2878`)

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?
PR incoming — guarded passthrough of the six Windows vars (`${VAR:+...}`, byte-identical env on Linux/macOS) + `PYTHONUTF8=1` (no-op where LANG already forces UTF-8). Verified: the failing collection above goes 16/16 green.

items.title: [Bug]: `hermes doctor` flags supported top-level config keys `group_sessions_per_user` and `known_plugin_toolsets` as unknown

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

`validate_config_structure()` in `hermes_cli/config.py` warns "Unknown top-level config key 'X' — it will be ignored" for two keys that Hermes itself supports at the top level of `config.yaml`:

- `group_sessions_per_user` — read from the top-level YAML by `gateway/config.py` and merged into the gateway configuration, so the "it will be ignored" claim is wrong; the gateway honors it.
- `known_plugin_toolsets` — written to `config.yaml` by Hermes' own toolset-save flow (`hermes_cli/tools_config.py`) to track which plugin toolsets each platform has seen, and read back by the same module. `hermes doctor` warns about a key Hermes wrote itself.

For `known_plugin_toolsets` the warning is also self-reinstating: deleting the key silences doctor only until the next `hermes tools` save writes it again (and deleting it is not harmless — its absence flips known-but-disabled plugin toolsets back to "new plugin, default enabled").

Before filing I searched open and closed issues and PRs for this and found no existing report, and confirmed the code on current `main` still has the mismatch (references below are to current HEAD).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the toolset picker (`hermes tools`) and save a platform toolset selection while a bundled plugin toolset (e.g. spotify) is present — Hermes writes `known_plugin_toolsets:` to `config.yaml`
2. Optionally also add `group_sessions_per_user: true` at the top level of `config.yaml` (a key `gateway/config.py` documents and reads)
3. Run `hermes doctor`

### Expected Behavior

Keys that Hermes itself reads or writes at the top level of `config.yaml` are in the known-roots allowlist and produce no Config Structure warning.

### Actual Behavior

```
◆ Config Structure
  ⚠ Unknown top-level config key 'group_sessions_per_user' — it will be ignored
    → Check for typos, or remove the key if it is not a supported config root. Run 'hermes doctor' for more detail.
  ⚠ Unknown top-level config key 'known_plugin_toolsets' — it will be ignored
    → Check for typos, or remove the key if it is not a supported config root. Run 'hermes doctor' for more detail.
```

Both keys are in fact honored (gateway) / maintained (toolset-save flow). The same warning also prints at CLI/gateway startup via `print_config_warnings()`.

### Affected Component

Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup), CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

`hermes debug share --local` system dump below. The log sections are omitted: this is a static config-validation allowlist mismatch, fully root-caused below, and the logs contain nothing relevant to it.

```
--- hermes dump ---
version:          0.18.2 [8fe9706d] (2026-07-19)
os:               Darwin 25.5.0 arm64
python:           3.11.15
openai_sdk:       2.24.0
profile:          default
hermes_home:      ~/.hermes
model:            Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-oQ6-fp16-mtp
provider:         omlx
terminal:         docker

api_keys:
  openrouter           not set
  openai               not set
  anthropic            not set
  anthropic_token      not set
  nous                 not set
  google/gemini        not set
  gemini               not set
  glm/zai              not set
  zai                  not set
  kimi                 not set
  minimax              not set
  deepseek             not set
  dashscope            not set
  huggingface          not set
  nvidia               not set
  opencode_zen         set
  opencode_go          not set
  kilocode             not set
  firecrawl            not set
  tavily               not set
  browserbase          not set
  fal                  not set
  elevenlabs           not set
  github               not set

features:
  toolsets:           hermes-cli
  mcp_servers:        0
  memory_provider:    built-in
  gateway:            running (launchd, pid 48672)
  platforms:          none
  cron_jobs:          5 active / 5 total
  skills:             2

config_overrides:
  terminal.backend: docker
  display.show_reasoning: False
  tts.provider: openai
  fallback_providers: [{'provider': 'opencode-zen', 'model': 'deepseek-v4-flash-free'}]
--- end dump ---
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0 arm64)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), install method git, upstream 8fe9706d

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS` in `hermes_cli/config.py` is `frozenset(DEFAULT_CONFIG.keys()) | _EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS` ([hermes_cli/config.py#L5520](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/hermes_cli/config.py#L5520)). Neither key is in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, and `_EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS` ([hermes_cli/config.py#L5501](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/hermes_cli/config.py#L5501)) — whose own comment says it exists for "roots read from the raw user YAML (or written by our own flows) that are intentionally absent from DEFAULT_CONFIG" — is missing both. So the unknown-key loop at the end of `validate_config_structure()` flags them.

Where each key is actually supported (current HEAD):

- [gateway/config.py#L1199-L1200](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/config.py#L1199-L1200) — top-level `group_sessions_per_user` merged into gateway config
- [gateway/config.py#L821](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/gateway/config.py#L821) — the documented field (default `True`)
- [hermes_cli/tools_config.py#L2006-L2010](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/hermes_cli/tools_config.py#L2006-L2010) — toolset-save flow writes top-level `known_plugin_toolsets`
- [hermes_cli/tools_config.py#L1853-L1856](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/hermes_cli/tools_config.py#L1853-L1856) — read back to distinguish "new plugin, default enabled" from "user disabled it"

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Add both keys to `_EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS`:

```python
    "group_sessions_per_user",   # top-level form read by gateway/config.py
    "known_plugin_toolsets",     # written by the hermes_cli/tools_config.py toolset-save flow
```

items.title: Compression warning can recommend a threshold below the small-context floor

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

The auxiliary-compression feasibility warning can recommend a `compression.threshold` value that Hermes will not actually honor.

For context windows below 512K, `ContextCompressor._effective_threshold_percent()` applies a hard-coded 75% raise-only floor. The warning in `conversation_compression.py` can independently calculate and recommend a lower value (for example, `0.73`). Setting that value still resolves to 75%, so the same warning returns on the next session.

## Reproduction

1. Use a main-model context window below 512K.
2. Use an auxiliary compression model whose context is below the main model's 75% compression threshold.
3. Start a session and observe the warning recommending a threshold below `0.75`.
4. Configure the recommended threshold.
5. Start another session.

The configured value is raised back to 75% by the small-context floor, and the auxiliary-context warning repeats.

## Expected behavior

The warning should account for the effective small-context floor before suggesting a threshold. If no viable threshold exists under the floor, it should omit that option and explain that a larger auxiliary model is required.

Alternatively, the floor could be documented and exposed as a configuration option for users who deliberately choose a lower threshold.

## Relevant behavior

- `context_compressor.py`: `_SMALL_CTX_WINDOW_LIMIT = 512_000` and `_SMALL_CTX_THRESHOLD_PERCENT = 0.75`
- `ContextCompressor._effective_threshold_percent()`: raises lower configured thresholds to 75%
- `conversation_compression.py`: warning recommendation is calculated separately and can suggest a value below the floor

## Possible fixes

- Calculate the warning recommendation using the same effective-threshold logic as `ContextCompressor`.
- Do not suggest `compression.threshold` when the required value is below the floor.
- Or provide/document a configuration option for the small-context floor.

items.title: tasks.model_override: no write surface, and the dispatcher's -m is discarded by the chat subparser

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
The kanban schema has a per-task `model_override` column ("When set, the dispatcher passes -m <model> to the worker", `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py` ~1140) and `kanban show` displays it. Two independent problems make the feature unusable in v0.18.0:

1. **No write surface.** Nothing sets the column: `hermes kanban create` has no `--model` option, `create_task()` has no model parameter, `kanban edit` only touches result/summary/metadata of done tasks, the agent-facing `kanban_create` tool and the dashboard `CreateTaskBody` have no model field. The only way to set it is a manual SQLite UPDATE.

2. **The dispatcher's `-m` is discarded anyway.** `_default_spawn` builds `hermes -p <profile> --accept-hooks -m <model> ... chat -q "work kanban task <id>"` (kanban_db.py ~7789), i.e. `-m` BEFORE the `chat` subcommand. The `chat` subparser redefines `-m/--model` with a `None` default, and on argparse of every supported Python (3.11-3.13, verified empirically) the subparser's default overwrites the top-level value in the merged namespace. So even a manually-set `model_override` reaches the worker as `None` and the worker falls back to its profile's `model.default`.

**Suggested fix**: add `--model` to `kanban create` (and the create tool), and either move the dispatcher's `-m` after the `chat` subcommand or set it via `HERMES_INFERENCE_MODEL` in the spawned process env.

items.title: Dashboard basic auth: unauthenticated visit 500s (single-provider redirect goes to the OAuth kick-off route)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main

**Setup**: dashboard bound to a non-loopback host with ONLY the bundled username/password provider configured (`dashboard.basic_auth` in config.yaml, as created by the interactive prompt in `cmd_dashboard`).

**Repro**: visit `http://<host>:<port>/` unauthenticated.

**Expected**: redirect to the login page with the password form.

**Actual**: HTTP 500. The unauthenticated middleware fast-path for a single session provider redirects to `/auth/login?provider=basic&next=%2F` (`hermes_cli/dashboard_auth/middleware.py` ~181-196). That route calls `provider.start_login()`, which for `BasicAuthProvider` raises `NotImplementedError` ("password-only; there is no OAuth redirect flow"), surfaced as a 500 to the browser.

**Workaround**: navigate to `/login` directly: the password form renders and works.

**Suggested fix**: in the single-provider fast-path, check `supports_password` and redirect to `{prefix}/login` for password-only providers instead of `/auth/login`.

items.body:
The fix in #4f67c3338 (`fix(config): whitelist real non-DEFAULT_CONFIG roots`) added `_EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS` but did **not** actually include the two keys this issue is about. On current `main` (`19527db73`):

```python
>>> from hermes_cli.config import _EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS
>>> 'group_sessions_per_user' in _EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS
False
>>> 'known_plugin_toolsets' in _EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS
False
```

So `hermes doctor` still warns:
```
⚠ Unknown top-level config key 'known_plugin_toolsets' — it will be ignored
```

Both keys are still missing from the allowlist that was supposed to silence them. Confirmed just now on a fresh v0.18.2 install at `19527db73` (post-update).

For `known_plugin_toolsets` the original report's point still stands: deleting the key to silence the warning is self-defeating — `hermes tools` writes it again (`tools_config.py:2012-2013`) and its absence flips known-but-disabled plugin toolsets back to "new plugin, default enabled". The warning is still firing against a key Hermes itself writes and reads.

Proposed completion of the fix — add both to `_EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS` in `hermes_cli/config.py` (around line 5504):

```python
_EXTRA_KNOWN_ROOT_KEYS = {
    ...
    "signal",
    # Keys read/written by Hermes flows but absent from DEFAULT_CONFIG:
    "group_sessions_per_user",    # top-level form read by gateway/config.py:1206
    "known_plugin_toolsets",      # written by `hermes tools` (tools_config.py:2012-2013)
}
```

Both are confirmed live read/write sites on current HEAD:
- `group_sessions_per_user`: `gateway/config.py:1206` (top-level bridge into `GatewayConfig`)
- `known_plugin_toolsets`: `hermes_cli/tools_config.py:1859` (read) + `:2012-2013` (write)

items.title: Telegram start_polling() wedges on initial poll acquisition (free slot) — gateway alive/heartbeat fresh, never acquires, 30s guard never fires (0.18.2)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
### Summary

On **0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2, upstream `f64e4f4f`)** the Telegram adapter **wedges on the *initial* poll acquisition**: a freshly-started gateway with a **free** `getUpdates` slot never acquires it. It sits forever on `[Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…` and never advances to a successful poll. The gateway process stays **alive and healthy** (cron ticker heartbeat updates every ~60s), so it looks up but is silently not serving. The `asyncio.wait_for(updater.start_polling(), timeout=_UPDATER_START_TIMEOUT=30.0)` guard (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` `_start_polling_resilient`, ~L2007) does **not** recover it.

This looks like the same family as #59614 / #66377 / #58790, but on the **initial-acquisition** path rather than a mid-ladder reconnect, and it **still reproduces on 0.18.2** (which predates the #66377 fix closed 2026-07-19).

### Environment
- hermes-agent **0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)**, `ghcr.io/hostinger/hvps-hermes-agent:latest`, Python 3.13, python-telegram-bot **22.6**.
- Containerized (Docker), Telegram-only gateway, `personal` profile.
- **Flaky/asymmetric egress to `api.telegram.org`**: broken IPv6 egress; IPv4 works. Mitigated with `extra_hosts` IPv4 pin + `network.force_ipv4: true` + `TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS` pin (skips DoH). The *same* 0.18.2 on two macOS hosts with clean egress polls flawlessly — so this is egress-environment-triggered.

### Key evidence (the wedge is NOT the network, NOT DoH, NOT HTTP/2)
From **inside the container**, against the live token:
- `curl -4 getMe` → 200 in 0.25s.
- **httpx** (the lib PTB uses) `getMe` → 200 in 0.4s; `getUpdates(timeout=0)` → 200 in 0.4s.
- **PTB directly** (`telegram.Bot` + `HTTPXRequest(connection_pool_size=512, pool_timeout=8.0)`): `initialize()` OK 0.3s; `delete_webhook()` OK 0.1s; `get_updates(timeout=0)` returns cleanly (a 409 Conflict when another instance holds the poll — i.e. it *reaches* getUpdates).

So `Bot`-level calls all work. Only the **`Updater.start_polling()` long-poll** (timeout>0) wedges on a free poll.

**py-spy dump** of the wedged gateway (`--nonblocking`, host-side against the container PID): MainThread **idle in `select()`** (`asyncio/base_events.py:_run_once` → `selectors.py:452`), **no thread in Telegram/httpx/DoH code** — i.e. a coroutine parked awaiting a network read that never returns. Cron/housekeeping threads all healthy.

### Behavioral asymmetry that pinpoints it
- When **another instance holds the poll** → the VPS gateway reaches getUpdates and logs **fast, steady 409 conflicts** (`polling conflict (1/5) … terminated by other getUpdates`). Healthy reach.
- When the **poll is free** (other instance stopped) → the *long-poll* getUpdates read **hangs**; it never acquires, no conflict, no timeout, stuck on `attempt 1/8`. `_UPDATER_START_TIMEOUT` guard never fires to recover.

### Impact
Gateway is “alive” (heartbeat fresh) but silently dead on the acquisition path; no self-recovery. On this deployment it makes a clean cutover to the VPS gateway impossible.

### Suspected cause / ask
The initial `start_polling()` long-poll read on a marginal egress link never completes and the 30s `wait_for` guard doesn’t interrupt it (coroutine parked in a way the guard can’t cancel, or the read timeout isn’t applied to the long-poll GET). Related to the CLOSE_WAIT / exhausted-pool family (#59614, #58790, #31599) and the reconnect-ladder stall (#66377), but on **first acquisition**. Is the #66377 fix expected to cover initial acquisition, and is it in any release after 0.18.2? A hard read-timeout on the long-poll GET (so a wedged read raises `TimedOut` → recovery ladder) would likely address it.

(Workaround being used meanwhile: Telegram **webhook mode** via `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL`, which bypasses long-polling entirely.)

items.title: Telegram gateway hangs at 'Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)' even after applying the #63309/#64370 TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS workaround — py-spy shows all threads idle, not blocked

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

On a fresh install of Hermes Agent v0.18.2, the Telegram gateway hangs indefinitely at `Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…` and never progresses — no crash, no "attempt 2/8", no timeout log, ever. This reproduces the symptom described in #63309, but persists **even after applying the `TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS` workaround** that let that report's reporter and the fix in #64370 sidestep the DNS-over-HTTPS discovery stall. Two independent `py-spy dump` captures (one before, one after applying the workaround) show **every thread idle** (`select()` / `wait()`), not a thread blocked in a synchronous frame — which is a different signature than the blocked-loop mechanism #64370 targeted, so I don't think this is the same root cause, just the same visible symptom.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream `1bf441cd`
- Fresh install via `install.sh --dir /opt/hermes --skip-setup --skip-browser --non-interactive` (repo manually pre-cloned into an empty target dir first, since the installer refuses to reuse any pre-existing directory — separate minor rough edge, happy to file separately if useful)
- Python 3.11.15 (uv-managed venv)
- Host: Ubuntu 24.04, KVM VPS, dual-stack IPv4 + IPv6 (native IPv6 `/64`, no VPN/proxy/TUN involved — this is a plain datacenter box, not a container-behind-a-proxy setup like #63309's environment)
- Running as a systemd service (`hermes gateway install --system --run-as-user <non-root user>`)
- Model/provider: `openrouter` / `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` — confirmed healthy and unrelated (`hermes doctor` shows "✓ OpenRouter API"); the hang is Telegram-adapter-specific.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install as above.
2. `hermes auth add openrouter --type api-key --api-key <key>` then set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in `.env` directly (note: `hermes auth add` alone did **not** satisfy `hermes doctor`'s "API key configured" check for OpenRouter — had to also set the plain env var; possibly worth a separate issue).
3. Set `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` and `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` in `~/.hermes/.env` (confirmed the token is valid via a direct `getMe` call before starting the gateway).
4. `hermes gateway install --system --run-as-user <user> --start-now`
5. `journalctl -u hermes-gateway` stalls forever at `Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…`.

## Sanity checks (ruling out network/DNS/credentials)

```
$ curl -4 -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' https://api.telegram.org
302 0.09s
$ curl -6 -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s\n' https://api.telegram.org
302 0.08s
$ curl -s https://api.telegram.org/bot<REDACTED>/getMe
{"ok":true,"result":{"id":...,"is_bot":true,"username":"Ampi12bot",...}}

$ /opt/hermes/venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import asyncio, httpx, time
async def main():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as c:
        t0=time.monotonic()
        r = await c.get("https://api.telegram.org/bot<REDACTED>/getMe")
        print(f"{time.monotonic()-t0:.2f}s {r.status_code}")
asyncio.run(main())
PY
0.06s 200
```
Same venv, same interpreter, same network namespace as the gateway process — instant success both ways.

## Applying the #63309/#64370 workaround (partial improvement, hang persists)

Set `TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS=149.154.166.110,2001:67c:4e8:f004::9` (both confirmed-reachable via the checks above) in `.env`. Result: the `Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…` log line **no longer appears** (confirms `self._fallback_ips()` short-circuits `discover_fallback_ips()` at `adapter.py:3512` as expected — only the IPv4 entry is kept, with `Ignoring non-IPv4 Telegram fallback IP: 2001:67c:4e8:f004::9` logged, also expected per `parse_fallback_ip_env`). But the gateway still hangs at the exact same `Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…` line, indefinitely — so the DoH discovery call was not (solely) responsible for this particular stall.

## py-spy evidence — both before and after the workaround, every thread is idle

Before (DoH discovery still active):
```
Thread <main> (idle): "MainThread"
    select (selectors.py:468)
    _run_once (asyncio/base_events.py:1898)
    run_forever (asyncio/base_events.py:608)
    run_until_complete (asyncio/base_events.py:641)
    run (asyncio/runners.py:118)
    run (asyncio/runners.py:190)
    run_gateway (hermes_cli/gateway.py:4980)
    ...
[all worker/watchdog threads: idle, in threading.wait() or ThreadPoolExecutor._worker idle]
```

After (TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS set, DoH discovery skipped) — **identical shape**:
```
Thread <main> (idle): "MainThread"
    select (selectors.py:468)
    _run_once (asyncio/base_events.py:1898)
    run_forever (asyncio/base_events.py:608)
    ... (same frames)
[all worker/watchdog threads: idle again]
```

No thread is ever caught executing a synchronous/blocking frame in either capture — the main thread is genuinely parked in `select()` with (apparently) nothing scheduled to wake it, and none of the background watchdog threads (`planned-stop-watcher`, `nous-auth-keepalive`, `cron-scheduler`, `gateway-housekeeping`) show anything unusual either. This looks less like "the loop is blocked" (what #64370's thread-deadline wrapper targets) and more like a task that silently completed, errored, or got orphaned without anything left to drive the next connection attempt or log the timeout — i.e. whatever is supposed to schedule "attempt 2/8" (or the 30s timeout message) after `Application.initialize()`'s first attempt never runs at all.

## Request

Could someone familiar with the `Application.initialize()` → attempt-retry loop in `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` take a look at what happens after the "Connecting to Telegram (attempt N/8)…" log line — specifically whether the coroutine/task driving the retry loop could silently exit (return, get cancelled, or swallow an exception) without either connecting successfully or logging the next attempt/timeout? Happy to add more instrumentation or test a patch against this environment — it's a clean, reproducible fresh install with nothing unusual about the network path.

items.title: Desktop: first message of a new chat dead-ends with "Prompt failed / session not found" when the draft's live session dies

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Symptom

Submitting the first message of a new chat in the desktop app can fail with a toast:

```
Prompt failed
session not found
```

The message is dropped, and re-submitting into the same chat fails the same way — there is no way forward for that draft.

## Root cause

Two designs interact badly for a chat that has never completed a first submit:

1. **The gateway persists a chat's `state.db` row lazily**, on its first successful `prompt.submit` (`_ensure_session_db_row`; `session.create` deliberately skips it so abandoned drafts never leave "Untitled" rows behind — see the comment in `tui_gateway/server.py` around the `session.create` handler).
2. **The desktop's sleep/wake recovery assumes the stored row exists.** In `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/submit.ts`, when `prompt.submit` fails with `4001 session not found` (stale live runtime id), the recovery calls `session.resume` with the stored id and retries. That `session.resume` call is **not wrapped in try/catch**.

For a first-submit draft there is no DB row, so the recovery `session.resume` rejects with `4007 session not found` — the rejection escapes to the outer catch and surfaces verbatim as the "Prompt failed / session not found" toast. The optimistic message is lost, and since the row still doesn't exist, every retry repeats the loop.

## Trigger

Any path that kills the live in-memory session between `session.create` and the first successful `prompt.submit`:

- sleep/wake or network blip: the WS drops (code 1006), the session is detached and torn down by the WS-orphan reaper after the grace window (`_schedule_ws_orphan_reap`), while the renderer still holds the stale runtime id;
- a gateway restart;
- a stale cached runtime id from a prior backend instance.

Observed in the wild on macOS: a session created + agent built at 19:40 with no turn ever running, `state.db` containing no row for it, and the failing submit surfacing exactly this toast.

## Why existing chats don't hit this

A chat with at least one successful turn has a DB row, so resume+retry recovery works (covered by the "sleep/wake session recovery" tests). The test suite covers "no stored id selected" and "non-404 submit errors", but not "the recovery resume itself 404s" — the only possible outcome for a never-persisted draft.

## Proposed fix

In the recovery path: catch the `session.resume` failure, and when **both** the live id and the stored row report "session not found" (the never-persisted-draft signature), mint a fresh backend session via `createBackendSessionForSend` and land the message there (re-homing the optimistic message, drift baseline, and attachment sync). Keep the surface-the-error behavior for timed-out submits (may have actually landed — re-sending elsewhere risks a double-send), non-404 resume failures (must not split a real stored chat in two, #55578 symptom b), and background queue drains (must never re-home the user's view).

PR incoming.

items.title: [Bug]: gateway run exits with SystemExit code 75 when no TTY is attached, causing a systemd restart loop (reproduced on two independent fresh installs)

items.body:
### Bug Description

When the gateway runs headless (systemd --user service, no controlling TTY), the process starts, connects all channels, runs for a few to ~20 minutes, then exits with SystemExit: 75 from gateway/run.py. The bundled unit's RestartForceExitStatus=75 immediately restarts it, producing an endless crash loop. In this loop, IMAP e-mail polling never completes a full cycle, so the Email gateway effectively never processes incoming mail (Telegram is also intermittently disrupted).
The exit outcome correlates strictly with whether a TTY is attached, per ~/.hermes/logs/gateway-exit-diag.log:

"stdin_is_tty": true → success: true / exit_clean
"stdin_is_tty": false → success: false / SystemExit code 75

Reproduced independently on two separate fresh installs (a Hetzner VPS and a NAS VM), so this is not a stale/leftover systemd unit — `hermes gateway install --force` regenerates the unit but does not fix it.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure the gateway with at least one channel (e.g. Telegram + Email).
2. Install the systemd `--user` service via `hermes gateway install` (or `--force`).
3. Start it and let it run headless (no TTY): `systemctl --user start hermes-gateway.service`.
4. Observe: after a few to ~20 minutes the process exits with code 75; systemd force-restarts it (`RestartForceExitStatus=75`), looping indefinitely.
5. Run the identical command with a TTY (`python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run` in a terminal) → runs cleanly, stays up.

### Expected Behavior

`gateway run` should run headless without a controlling TTY and exit 0 on clean shutdown. The bundled systemd unit should keep the service stably running without depending on a PTY.


### Actual Behavior

Headless runs exit with `SystemExit: 75` after some runtime and enter a restart loop via `RestartForceExitStatus=75`. E-mail polling never completes; the service is effectively unusable as a daemon.
Traceback (from `gateway-exit-diag.log`):
```
File "gateway/run.py", line 22297, in start_gateway
    raise SystemExit(runner.exit_code)
SystemExit: 75
```

(On a slightly older build the same failure occurred at `gateway/run.py:21664 `— line differs by version, behavior identical.)

Workaround (confirmed working):
Wrapping ExecStart in a real PTY fixes it. `setsid --wait …` was not sufficient; `script` works:
```
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/usr/bin/script -qefc "…/venv/bin/python -m hermes_cli.main gateway run" /dev/null
```

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (VM on NAS) — also reproduced on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Hetzner VPS)

3.11.15

v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)

```shell

```

_No response_

items.title: Hermes Desktop v0.18.2 — 8 Core Architectural Failures

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
**Version:** v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), git 36f2a966, Windows 10, Electron Desktop app

---

### 1. Sessions leak between profile databases

The desktop app writes sessions to the root `state.db` regardless of which profile is active. Root DB (97MB) has 57 sessions, 7,271 messages — 0% tagged with a profile name. Personal profile DB (68MB) has 537 sessions, 93% untagged.

**11 session IDs are duplicated** across both databases with different content — same ID, different messages. When session resume reads from the wrong DB, it finds an empty stub instead of real history. This is why users "lose their last output."

### 2. Memory char limit ignored, profiles cross-contaminated

Config sets `memory_char_limit: 15000`. Actual MEMORY.md is **22,997 bytes (53% over)** — the limit is never enforced on write. Both profiles have identical memory files (same md5 hash, same modification timestamp to the sub-second). Memory writes go to both profiles' stores simultaneously, defeating profile isolation entirely.

### 3. Honcho integration charged per action then silently broke

Honcho was configured as `provider: honcho`. Every memory write was a paid API call to Honcho's cloud. Account `andyjcopson2@gmail.com` accumulated ~$99.02 in charges. OAuth expired, the integration broke silently, and Honcho kept billing. Config now has `provider: ""`. The user was forced to compensate by overfilling the built-in memory, which then overflowed (see Issue 2). The agent reports "saved to memory" when the write silently fails.

### 4. Aggressive compression destroys context

```yaml
compression:
  threshold: 0.5
  target_ratio: 0.2
  protect_first_n: 3  # only 3 messages survive
  protect_last_n: 20
```

45% of all root DB messages are compacted (3,283 of 7,275). Worst case: **1,197 of 1,468 messages compressed (82%)**. `protect_first_n: 3` destroys the conversation foundation. Combined with Issue 1, by the time a user returns to a session, most context is gone. The agent gets measurably worse over time.

### 5. Daily 4am auto-reset erases work without consent

```yaml
session_reset:
  mode: both
  idle_minutes: 1440  # 24h idle
  at_hour: 4          # force-reset daily at 4am
```

Every day at 4am all sessions are force-reset. With session routing broken (Issue 1), finding and resuming yesterday's work is unreliable.

### 6. Chats reappear after deletion or archiving

42 sessions are archived in personal DB (`archived=1`). **0 sessions are archived in root DB.** Archive/delete operations only touch the profile DB — the root DB copy is untouched. 6 confirmed overlapping session IDs have `archived=0` in root DB. **299 zero-message session stubs** exist in personal DB, appearing as empty active sessions that can't be removed.

### 7. Profile config isolation doesn't exist

`profiles/personal/config.yaml` does not exist. Personal profile inherits root `config.yaml` directly. Model/provider settings cannot differ per profile. Switching profiles is cosmetic.

### 8. Fresh installs don't help

All bugs are in shipped source code at `apps/desktop/` and the core Python memory module. Clean reinstalls reproduce the same failures. User cannot self-remediate.

---

**Net result:** The software actively fights the user — splitting sessions across two databases, silently failing to save, compressing away context, resetting daily, sharing memory between profiles, and undoing archive/delete actions. It gets worse with use. This is not user error or configuration; these are shipped architectural defects in the profile/session/memory systems.

items.title: [Bug]: CLI continuous voice — record hotkey (Ctrl+B) ignored during STT/agent; only /voice off exits loop

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
### Bug Description

```markdown
### Summary

In **CLI interactive voice mode** with **continuous recording**, the configured record hotkey (default **Ctrl+B**) only exits continuous mode while `_voice_recording` is true. During **transcription** (`_voice_processing`) and while the **agent is running**, the same hotkey is a **silent no-op** and does **not** clear continuous mode. After the turn, recording auto-restarts. The only reliable way to stop the STT/voice loop is **`/voice off`**.

This makes continuous voice feel “stuck”: repeated Ctrl+B appears to do nothing, and typing `/voice off` is hard because the session keeps re-entering record/STT/agent cycles.

Docs say continuous ends when you press the record key **during recording**. That works only in a narrow REC window. Users reasonably expect the stop hotkey (or any explicit stop intent) to **disarm continuous** even if silence auto-stop already moved them into STT or an agent turn.

### Environment (reporter)

- Hermes Agent **v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)** (confirm with `hermes --version`)
- Install: git clone under `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` (method: git)
- Python **3.11.x**
- OS: Linux
- Surface: **CLI only** (`hermes` / profile chat — not TUI gateway, not messaging gateway)
- STT: local / `local_command` (repro does not require a specific provider)

Note: install may not be tip-of-main; behavior is in current `cli.py` continuous voice logic. Happy to retest on a newer build if maintainers want confirmation.
```

### Steps to Reproduce

```markdown
1. Start CLI chat: `hermes` (or profile-equivalent interactive CLI).
2. Enable voice: `/voice on`.
3. Press **Ctrl+B** (or configured `voice.record_key`) to start recording.
4. Speak a short phrase; stop speaking and wait for **silence auto-stop**.
5. When the UI shows **transcribing** (or immediately after, while the agent is busy on the transcript), press **Ctrl+B** several times.
6. Wait for the agent turn to finish.
7. Observe whether recording **auto-restarts** without another intentional start.
8. Try to stop the loop with Ctrl+B again during agent / STT phases.
9. Run `/voice off` — this successfully disables voice and stops the cycle.

**Optional amplifier (not required):** leave continuous voice on with TTS playing through open speakers so the mic re-triggers often — the “dead zone” becomes the common case, but the bug reproduces without TTS.
```

### Expected Behavior

```markdown
- Pressing the record hotkey with continuous voice active should **always express stop intent** for the continuous loop:
  - If recording: stop the take (and clear continuous), as documented.
  - If transcribing or agent-busy with continuous still armed: **clear continuous** so the loop does not auto-restart after the current work finishes.
- Ideally the hotkey never **silently** no-ops while continuous mode is still ON.
- `/voice status` (or equivalent) should make continuous ON/OFF visible (today status shows mode/TTS/recording but not continuous).
- Behavior should be consistent with the TUI continuous API intent (`hermes_cli.voice.stop_continuous`), which already has tests around mid-transcription stop not restarting the loop.
```

### Actual Behavior

```markdown
- Ctrl+B **while recording**: clears continuous and stops/transcribes (works in that window only).
- Ctrl+B **while `_voice_processing` (STT)**: handler returns without clearing continuous → **no user-visible effect**.
- Ctrl+B **while `_agent_running` and not recording**: start path returns early → **no effect**; continuous remains true.
- After the agent turn completes, continuous still true → **auto-restart recording**.
- Only **`/voice off`** reliably tears down mode + continuous + recorder.
- Typing `/voice off` often takes several attempts because the UI keeps cycling record/STT/agent.
```

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
<!-- Prefer privacy-safe local output -->


hermes debug share --local
# redact secrets / absolute personal paths before paste


If upload is acceptable after scrubbing:


hermes debug share
# paste the printed Report / agent.log links
```

### Operating System

Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
No crash or traceback — pure control-flow / UX bug.

Observational cues:
- Status / placeholder cycles: recording → "transcribing..." → agent busy placeholder → recording again.
- `/voice status` shows Mode ON and Recording flipping yes/no while continuous restarts continue.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

```markdown
### CLI continuous state machine (`cli.py`)

Voice continuous mode is implemented with CLI-local flags:

- `_voice_recording`
- `_voice_processing`
- `_voice_continuous`

Record hotkey handler (`handle_voice_record`):

1. If `_voice_recording`: set `_voice_continuous = False`, dispatch `_voice_stop_and_transcribe`.
2. Else (not recording):
   - If `_agent_running`: **return** (no continuous clear).
   - If `_voice_processing`: **return** (no continuous clear).
   - Else: set `_voice_continuous = True` and start recording.

So **stop intent only clears continuous in the recording branch**. During STT and agent turns — often most of a busy voice session — the hotkey does not disarm continuous.

After a successful turn, process_loop auto-restarts recording when:

- `_voice_mode` and `_voice_continuous` and not `_voice_recording`

…optionally waiting on `_voice_tts_done` when Hermes voice TTS is enabled.

### Docs vs behavior

User guide (voice mode): continuous continues until Ctrl+B **during recording** or 3 consecutive no-speech cycles. That matches the narrow branch, but is easy to miss in practice when silence auto-stop immediately leaves the REC state.

### CLI vs TUI asymmetry

- **TUI gateway** uses `hermes_cli.voice.start_continuous` / `stop_continuous`.
- **`hermes_cli.voice`** includes continuous control with tests such as mid-transcription stop must not restart the loop (`tests/hermes_cli/test_voice_wrapper.py`).
- **Classic CLI PTT path does not use that API** for the continuous loop; it keeps the older flag machine in `cli.py`.

This looks like incomplete convergence: TUI got a clearer continuous API; CLI continuous exit still has silent dead zones.
```

---

## Proposed Fix (optional — include)

```markdown
### Minimum fix (CLI)

In `handle_voice_record`, when voice mode is on:

- **Any** press while continuous is active (or always when voice mode is on and user intends stop) should set `_voice_continuous = False`.
- If recording: existing stop/transcribe path.
- If processing: do not silent-return without clearing continuous; optionally cancel/discard restart (mirror `stop_continuous` semantics).
- If agent running and not recording: allow **disarm continuous** without starting a new take (today start is blocked, but continuous should still clear).

### Product polish

- `/voice status`: show `Continuous: ON|OFF`.
- Avoid silent no-ops: dim status line “continuous disarmed” / “ignored: already stopping”.

### Longer-term

- Drive CLI continuous from `hermes_cli.voice` so CLI and TUI share one state machine and the existing unit tests.

I am reporting from production CLI use; I can retest a PR/patch if useful. A full PR from me is optional / not promised in this issue.
```

---

## Suggested first comment (if you want a short public note after filing)

```markdown
Filed from real CLI continuous-voice use (local STT). Happy to retest on main or try a proposed patch. Not a gateway/messaging issue — pure interactive CLI.
```

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Minimal fix in CLI `handle_voice_record` (`cli.py`):

When voice mode is on and the user is NOT currently recording, if
`_voice_continuous` or `_voice_processing` is true, clear
`_voice_continuous = False` and return — do not silent-return and do not
start a new take.

Today continuous is only cleared in the `_voice_recording` branch, so
Ctrl+B during STT/agent leaves continuous armed and process_loop
auto-restarts recording after the turn.

This is ~10–15 lines, CLI-only, no STT/TTS provider changes. Aligns with
`hermes_cli.voice.stop_continuous` / TUI intent (disarm without restart).
Full CLI migration onto `hermes_cli.voice` can be a follow-up.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.body:
## Problem

After running `hermes update`, the Hermes Desktop shortcut shows:

> The item 'Hermes.exe' that this shortcut refers to has been changed or moved, so this shortcut will no longer work properly.

The `Hermes.exe` binary was deleted during the update but the rebuild failed, leaving no executable at `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe`.

## Root Cause

After the update, `@assistant-ui` packages (react, store, tap, core) were missing from `node_modules/`. Running `npm run build --prefix apps/desktop` failed with:

```
Error: [vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "@assistant-ui/react" from "...status.tsx"
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes version: 0.18.2
- Node.js: installed via hermes-agent repo

## Fix (manual)

```bash
cd "%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent"
npm ci
npm run build --prefix apps/desktop
npm run --prefix apps/desktop builder -- --win --dir
```

## Notes

- This may be related to PR #46707 which pinned `@assistant-ui/store` to 0.2.13
- The update flow appears to wipe `node_modules` or build artifacts without ensuring `npm ci` completes before attempting the desktop rebuild
- Cron jobs, gateway, and CLI continued working — only the Desktop GUI was affected

items.title: kanban: worker-created scratch children inherit parent workspace path

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### What happened?

A dispatcher-spawned Kanban worker that calls the `kanban_create` tool without workspace arguments silently copies its own task's `workspace_kind` **and literal `workspace_path`** to the new task. When the parent is a managed `scratch` task, the child row therefore points at the parent's already-materialized scratch directory instead of getting its own `<board>/workspaces/<child-id>` directory at dispatch.

That breaks the documented isolation boundary: a remediation child can mutate or switch branches inside an earlier independent-review workspace, invalidating the review evidence and allowing concurrent tasks to share one checkout/index.

The root is `tools/kanban_tools.py::_handle_create`: `_inherit_workspace` is true whenever the caller omits both workspace fields, and lines currently assign both values from `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK`'s row without distinguishing managed scratch paths from explicitly shared directories.

### Production-adjacent evidence

Observed on 2026-07-19:

- Parent review task `t_9fa054e8`: `workspace_kind=scratch`, path `.../workspaces/t_9fa054e8`.
- Worker-created remediation child `t_17d5f85f`: `workspace_kind=scratch`, but the same literal parent path `.../workspaces/t_9fa054e8`.
- The child then edited a checkout inside the rejected-review directory. A separately created successor review remained unmaterialized (`workspace_path=NULL`), isolating the defect to worker-created tool children rather than all task creation.

### Expected behavior

- Omitted/default `scratch` workspace means an unmaterialized child (`workspace_path=NULL`) that resolves to its own deterministic `<board>/workspaces/<child-id>` directory.
- Nested worker-created children preserve that invariant.
- Independent-review children never inherit an implementer's/rejected-review directory by default.
- Sharing a persistent directory remains supported only when the creator explicitly passes `workspace_kind=dir` plus `workspace_path`.
- Project-linked children may inherit the project identity, but must materialize their own task worktree/path.
- CLI, dashboard/API, retry/reclaim, goal-mode, and decompose behavior must remain consistent and existing rows stay readable.

### Overlap check

- #61911 / #61907 address decomposed **worktree** siblings sharing a checkout; PR #61907 explicitly leaves `dir`/`scratch` inheritance unchanged.
- #65953 isolates `delegate_task` children from Kanban ownership; it does not cover a new Kanban task created through `kanban_create` by a running Kanban worker.

Neither current lane covers this worker-created default-scratch path inheritance.

### Proposed test plan

1. In a temporary `HERMES_HOME`, create and claim a scratch parent with its materialized path recorded.
2. Call `_handle_create` with no workspace args and assert current `main` reproduces the inherited literal path (RED).
3. Assert the fixed child remains `scratch` with `workspace_path is None`, resolves to its own task-id path, and cannot write into the parent's evidence directory through dispatcher context.
4. Cover nested child, explicit scratch, explicit `dir` sharing, project/worktree inheritance without literal path reuse, CLI/dashboard defaults, retries/reclaims, goal mode, and decompose sibling behavior.

Related Kanban implementation task: focused upstream fix only; no live DB migration or local runtime rollout.

items.title: Desktop: user messages duplicated and stacked at bottom after model switch

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

After a model switch occurs mid-session, user messages appear **duplicated** and **stacked at the bottom** of the chat. The same user message renders twice in the Desktop UI, even though the DB contains only one copy.

## Environment

- **OS**: macOS 27.0 (Sequoia)
- **Hermes Desktop** (app.asar rebuilt `2026-07-19 21:17 CST`)
- **Model switches**: deepseek-v4-pro → glm-5.2 → deepseek-v4-pro
- **Session**: `20260720_004624_29ee42`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a Desktop session
2. Switch model mid-session (e.g. via `/model`)
3. Continue the conversation
4. Observe the chat view — real user messages are duplicated, and all user messages appear clustered at the bottom

## Actual Behavior

6 user messages appear as cards at the bottom. **Card 1 and Card 2 are identical** (`这几个问题你确认一下，确认清楚后直接推进逐项自验。`). The same text renders twice.

## Expected Behavior

Each user message should render exactly once.

## Root Cause Analysis (confirmed)

### DB layer — NOT the cause
Verified `state.db` for session `20260720_004624_29ee42`: **zero duplicate messages**. Every user message exists exactly once:

```
rowid=94831 | user | 你能不能检查一下我们定时任务所有的代码文件...
rowid=94883 | user | [System: The active model for this chat has changed to glm-5.2...]
rowid=94889 | user | 这几个问题你确认一下...         ← only ONE copy in DB
rowid=94944 | user | 你确认清楚，确认清楚后...
rowid=94970 | user | [System: The active model for this chat has changed to deepseek-v4-pro...]
rowid=94971 | user | 我们今天的对话为什么...
```

### Rendering layer — root cause
Model switch notifications (`[System: The active model has changed to...]`) are stored with `role=user` in the DB. This is pre-existing behavior (confirmed since 7/17).

When the Desktop rendering pipeline encounters these `role=user` System messages interspersed with real user messages, it **duplicates the subsequent real user message**. The System message is consumed/hidden, but the rendering state counter advances incorrectly, causing the next real message to render twice.

### Suspect commits
The Desktop app was rebuilt on **7/19 21:17** (confirmed via `app.asar` mtime), which pulled in upstream performance optimizations including:

- `9b8b054c2` — "perf: fast model picker + dialogs — **off-screen turns skip rendering**"
- `0f05aaa2b` — "perf(desktop): make session switching snappy on large transcripts"
- `c856f3645` — "perf(desktop): kill the layout-thrash cascade on session switch"

These rendering optimizations likely introduced the off-by-one error when processing `role=user` messages that contain System notifications.

## Verification

This is NOT the same as:
- #63679 (assistant messages rendering twice — streaming intermediate leak)
- #65293 (CLI resume duplicates Previous Conversation)

This is specifically: Desktop UI duplicates **user** messages when `[System:]` notifications (stored as `role=user`) are present in the message stream.

items.title: [Bug]: search_files with absolute Windows path fails — _bash_safe_path rewrites D:\ to /d/ which native rg cannot resolve (IO error 3)

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary
On native Windows (no WSL), `search_files` fails whenever an **absolute Windows path** is passed. The path is rewritten to MSYS form (`D:\...` or `D:/...` → `/d/...`) by `_bash_safe_path`, but the bundled/WinGet `rg` is a **native Windows** binary that only understands `D:/` and `D:\`, not `/d/`. Result: `rg: ... IO error ... The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)`.

Relative paths work (they are not rewritten). The workaround is to use `terminal` + `rg "D:/..."` directly. But the system prompt tells agents to prefer `search_files` over `grep/rg`, so this is a real trap.

## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 / Windows native (no WSL)
- Hermes version: `Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 299e409f` (install method: git)
- ripgrep: `ripgrep 15.1.0 (rev af60c2de9d)` (native Windows binary, from WinGet at `C:\Users\ivo\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\rg`)
- Shell: Git Bash (MSYS)

## Steps to reproduce
1. In a chat on native Windows, call:
   `search_files(path="D:\IvoDimitrov-Universe\Apps\The-Pulse\data\ai-costs.json", pattern="subscription", target="content")`
   (also fails with `D:/...` form)
2. Tool returns error: `rg: /d/IvoDimitrov-Universe/Apps/The-Pulse/data/ai-costs.json: IO error for operation on /d/IvoDimitrov-Universe/Apps/The-Pulse/data/ai-costs.json: The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3)`

## Expected behavior
`search_files` resolves the absolute Windows path and returns matches, the same way `rg "D:/IvoDimitrov-Universe/..."` works when run directly via `terminal`.

## Root cause (verified by reading the source)
- `tools/file_operations.py` → `SearchFileOps._search_with_rg` builds `rg` and passes the path through `_escape_shell_arg` → `tools/environments/local.py:_bash_safe_path`.
- `_bash_safe_path` explicitly converts native `C:\Users\x` / `C:/Users/x` → `/c/Users/x` (MSYS form), because the shell is Git Bash and bash strips backslashes.
- That `/d/...` string is then handed to the **native Windows `rg`**, which does not understand MSYS paths → `os error 3`.
- `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` does **not** help, because the `/d/` rewrite happens in Python (`_bash_safe_path`) before bash ever sees the argument.

## Why this matters / workaround
- Relative paths inside the working dir work (e.g. `search_files(path="Apps/The-Pulse", ...)`).
- Direct `terminal` + `rg "D:/..."` works.
- So the defect is specific to the absolute-path rewrite path in `search_files`. Agents are told to use `search_files` instead of `rg`, so they hit this immediately on Windows.

## Suggested fix (non-breaking)
In `tools/environments/local.py:_bash_safe_path`, skip the `/c/...` rewrite when the resolved consumer is `rg` (which is invoked through `shell=True`/Git Bash but is a native Windows exe). Either:
- detect the `rg` invocation and pass `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL=*` / `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` only for that subprocess, or
- normalize to `D:/...` (forward-slash Windows form) instead of `/d/...` when the downstream binary is `rg`, since native `rg` accepts `D:/...`.

Related: issue #16201 (general Windows path-handling class) and #17753 (different symptom: read_file/terminal cannot find local file). This report is for the specific `search_files` + `rg` IO error 3 case, which is not covered by those.

## Labels
type/bug, tool/file, platform/windows, P2 Medium — degraded but workaround exists

items.title: Spurious TUI "stdin EOF" persists after d1f23bb2: O_NONBLOCK on a shared open file description, not a closed pipe; stdin guard misses ~/.hermes/plugins/

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Spurious TUI `stdin EOF` still happens on current `main` (which contains `d1f23bb2`). I instrumented a live failure: **nothing closed the pipe and nothing consumed stdin — the socket was alive with the peer still open.** The mechanism is `O_NONBLOCK` on a **shared open file description**, laundered into EOF by CPython's buffered layer.

`stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` is the correct fix (it unshares the description, so a child's flag lands on its own devnull). But the explanatory model attached to this bug family is wrong — #33299's "some subprocess consumes stdin data or closes the pipe's write end" is impossible as written: a child inherits only the gateway's end and never holds the TUI's write end, and consuming data yields silence, not EOF. That wrong model is why three gaps stayed open.

## Evidence

Forensics at the moment of a live failure:

```
startup={'ino': 14290115, 'mode': '0o140777', 'link': 'socket:[14290115]'}
eagain-state: O_NONBLOCK=True SO_RCVTIMEO=0.0 SO_TYPE=1
fd0:    ino=14290115   <- unchanged, not swapped
anchor: ino=14290115   <- dup() from startup, pins the original description
anchor read: EWOULDBLOCK — original socket ALIVE, peer still open
socket holders: ['pid=4045721 python3 -m tui_gateway.entry',
                 'pid=4046447 node .../ori add <id> --type insight']
```

Parent side, same incident — inode identical at spawn and teardown, `writableEnded=false`, so the TUI never called `end()`:

```
[stdin-debug] spawn:    fd=24 ino=14290114
[stdin-debug] destroy() fd=24 ino=14290114   at ChildProcess._handle.onexit
[lifecycle]   child exit exitCode=0 signal=null
```

`EWOULDBLOCK` rather than `b''` is decisive: a closed or half-closed `SOCK_STREAM` peer returns `b''` even in non-blocking mode.

## Mechanism

1. A subprocess inherits fd 0. Under `--tui` that is an `AF_UNIX` socketpair to the TUI parent.
2. It sets `O_NONBLOCK`. **That flag lives on the open file description, not the descriptor**, so it lands on the gateway's own stdin. This is standard libuv behavior for socket-type stdio, not a quirk of one tool — which is why the blast radius is *any Node CLI spawned with inherited stdio* (npm in #33299, `ori` here).
3. The gateway's next `read()` returns `EAGAIN`. On 3.11.15: `FileIO.read -> None`, `BufferedReader.read1 -> b''`, `TextIOWrapper.readline -> ''`, iteration -> `StopIteration`.
4. `for raw in sys.stdin` falls through to `_log_exit("stdin EOF (TUI closed the command pipe)")`, exit 0.

Minimal repro — socketpair stdin, peer held open, nothing ever written:

```python
CHILD = r"""
import fcntl, os, sys
fcntl.fcntl(0, fcntl.F_SETFL, fcntl.fcntl(0, fcntl.F_GETFL) | os.O_NONBLOCK)
n = 0
for raw in sys.stdin:
    n += 1
print(f"RESULT=clean-fallthrough lines={n}", flush=True)
"""
parent_end, child_end = socket.socketpair()
proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", CHILD], stdin=child_end.fileno(),
                        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
child_end.close()          # parent_end stays OPEN
print(proc.communicate()[0])
```

```
RESULT=clean-fallthrough lines=0 / exit_code=0 / peer_still_open=True
```

**Scope note:** this is proven for my incident, and strong inference for #33299 (npm is Node). I am *not* claiming it explains #14036 — that report's strace shows a `SIGPIPE` flood, which `EAGAIN` cannot produce, so it involved at least one additional mechanism.

## Why the distinction matters

- **It's a race with a ~0.3s window.** The child sets the flag ~0.14s after spawn and restores it ~0.4s later on clean exit. Only a `read()` *entering* that window dies; an already-blocked read is immune. So a fast, clean, successful subprocess still kills the gateway intermittently, and nothing aimed at timeouts, signals, or child lifetime helps.
- **Leaks need no `SIGKILL`.** Two overlapping children reproduce a lost update with two clean exits: the second snapshots stdio flags while the first's window is open, then faithfully restores non-blocking. The flag stays set with no process left to blame.
- **stdout is equally exposed.** The flag lands on whichever stdio fd is a socket. A child inheriting fd 1 puts `EAGAIN` on the JSON-RPC channel, and `tui_gateway/transport.py:36-43` re-raises `OSError` whose errno isn't in `_PEER_GONE_ERRNOS` — `EAGAIN` isn't.
- **Frames can be truncated, not just terminated.** A flip landing mid-line yields a partial line with no `\n`, surfacing as a spurious `-32700 parse error`.

## Gap 1 — the guard cannot see user plugins

`scripts/check_subprocess_stdin.py:144` resolves roots repo-relative:

```python
for tui_dir in TUI_CONTEXT_DIRS:      # "agent/", "tools/", "plugins/", "tui_gateway/"
    dirpath = repo_root / tui_dir
```

`plugins/` is the **bundled** dir. Per `hermes_cli/plugins.py:10-12`, plugins also load from `~/.hermes/plugins/` and `./.hermes/plugins/`, never scanned. My failure came from `~/.hermes/plugins/ori/hooks.py`, whose hook fires from `agent/turn_finalizer.py:563` **inside the gateway process** and spawned `ori` with all three stdio fds inherited. The guard exits 0 while that ships. `tests/tools/test_subprocess_stdin_guard.py` just re-runs the same script at the same scope, and the loader does no validation.

The regex at `:76` also misses `subprocess.call`, `check_output`, `os.system`, and `asyncio.create_subprocess_*`.

## Gap 2 — no gateway-side defense

Per-call-site discipline can't cover third-party or user-plugin code. The gateway can tell the two cases apart itself, since a spurious EOF leaves `O_NONBLOCK` set and a genuine one doesn't:

```python
while True:
    for raw in sys.stdin:
        ...                     # existing body unchanged
    if not (fcntl.fcntl(0, fcntl.F_GETFL) & os.O_NONBLOCK):
        break                   # flag clear -> real EOF -> exit as before
    os.set_blocking(0, True)    # spurious -> restore and resume the same sys.stdin
```

EOF is not sticky in `_io`, so iteration resumes. Verified against a live third-party flip: message before the flip handled, recovery logged, message *after* the flip handled, clean exit 0 only on genuine peer close.

Two caveats: as written it retries unbounded, so add a recovery-rate cap; and `F_GETFL` only sees the `O_NONBLOCK` variant — a child setting `SO_RCVTIMEO` (a socket option, equally shared, which times out even a blocking read) launders into the same spurious EOF with the flag clear. Checking `getsockopt(SO_RCVTIMEO)` alongside closes that too.

## Gap 3 — the log message asserts a cause

`reason=stdin EOF (TUI closed the command pipe)` is hardcoded and was false in every instance here. It sends investigations hunting the TUI parent. Better to report the observation and include `O_NONBLOCK` / `SO_RCVTIMEO` / peer state.

## Environment

- Hermes `main` @ `36f2a966c` (contains `d1f23bb2`, so this is *after* the broad fix)
- Python 3.11.15, Node v22.23.0, Linux
- Trigger: `~/.hermes/plugins/ori/hooks.py` calling `subprocess.run(["ori", "add", ...], timeout=10)` with no `stdin=`

Locally fixed by adding `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` to the plugin's three spawns (plus `stdout`/`stderr` on the one inheriting fd 1) and adding the resume loop above.
