items.title: [Bug]: .hermes/hermes-agent/run.py is 23,006 lines of code

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

`gateway/run.py` is a **23,006-line, 1.06 MB single file** - confirmed at Hermes v0.18.2 (commit on `main` as of 2026-07-20). It is the gateway's entry point, runtime orchestrator, message router, sanitization layer, resume-recovery logic, cache manager, signal handler, and housekeeping loop, all in one module.

This is not a cosmetic complaint. A single 1 MB module harms every contributor and every production trait: test coverage, review quality, CI feedback time, and merge-conflict rate.

### Evidence (v0.18.2, `gateway/run.py`)

- **Total lines:** 23,006
- **File size:** 1,116,370 bytes (1.06 MB)
- **Top-level functions (`def` / `async def`):** 91
- **Top-level classes:** 3 (`MultiplexConfigError`, `SecondaryPortBindingConfigError`, **`GatewayRunner`**)
- **`GatewayRunner` class spans:** L3028 to end - roughly 20,000 lines inside one class
- **Statement coverage:** **53.85%** (below the 70% project threshold - see #36353)

For comparison, the next largest file in `gateway/` is `platforms/base.py` at 256 KB - **less than a quarter the size**. `run.py` is an outlier by 4x.

## Why this matters (concrete impact)

1) **Coverage is stuck at 53.85%.** Issue #36353 has been open since the module was ~9.2k statements; adding tests to a 23k-line module is disproportionately expensive because fixtures must bootstrap the whole gateway runtime. Splitting the module into focused units makes targeted unit tests possible.
2) **Review and merge friction.** Every gateway-touching PR re-opens this file. Conflicts and review latency scale with file size.
3) **Cognitive load.** A reviewer landing on `run.py` for the first time has no entry point: the file mixes unrelated concerns (secret redaction, media typing, Telegram command-name sanitization, resume-recovery notes, PID-file locking, cron ticker setup) that have nothing to do with each other.
4) **Slow editor/indexer performance.** 1 MB Python files degrade IDE navigation, grep, and linter throughput for every contributor.

## The proven pattern already exists

`GatewayRunner` **already** inherits from three mixins, each in its own file:

```
class GatewayRunner(
    GatewayAuthorizationMixin,     # gateway/authz_mixin.py        (37 KB)
    GatewayKanbanWatchersMixin,    # gateway/kanban_watchers.py    (65 KB)
    GatewaySlashCommandsMixin,     # gateway/slash_commands.py     (236 KB)
):
```

This is the extraction vector that has demonstrably worked. The body of `GatewayRunner` still holds ~20k lines of methods that can follow the same path. The community has already started this work:

- **#55304** - extract display helpers to `gateway/display_helpers.py` (open)
- **#55190** - extract text sanitization to `gateway/text_sanitizer.py` (open)
- **#62880** - extract cached-agent state mixin (open)

## Proposed decomposition

A staged, behavior-preserving extraction along existing functional seams. Each stage ships independently and is verifiable by green tests + no diff in gateway behavior.

**Stage 1 - module-level helpers** (no `GatewayRunner` changes, lowest risk):
- `_redact_*`, `_GATEWAY_SECRET_PATTERNS`, `_gateway_provider_error_*`, `_looks_like_gateway_provider_error`, `_sanitize_gateway_final_response`, `_prepare_gateway_status_message` -> `gateway/text_sanitizer.py` (already proposed in #55190)
- `_resolve_gateway_display_bool`, `_has_platform_display_override`, `_telegramize_command_mentions`, `render_notice_line` -> `gateway/display_helpers.py` (already proposed in #55304)
- `_event_media_*`, `_build_media_placeholder`, `_build_document_context_note`, `_probe_audio_duration`, `_format_duration` -> `gateway/media_utils.py`
- `build_resume_recovery_note`, `_build_replay_entry`, `_build_gateway_agent_history`, `_select_cached_agent_history`, `_coerce_gateway_timestamp`, `_is_fresh_gateway_interruption`, `_auto_continue_freshness_window` -> `gateway/resume_recovery.py`
- `_run_planned_stop_watcher`, `_start_gateway_housekeeping`, `_start_cron_ticker`, `_await_thread_exit`, shutdown-forensics wiring -> `gateway/lifecycle.py`
- `_ensure_windows_gateway_venv_imports`, `_exit_after_graceful_shutdown` -> `gateway/entry.py`

**Stage 2 - `GatewayRunner` methods to mixins** (follows the authz/kanban/slash precedent):
- Cache-busting / agent-cache logic (`_extract_cache_busting_config`, `_enforce_agent_cache_cap`, `_session_expiry_watcher`) -> `GatewayCacheMixin` - this also resolves #33381 (Honcho-specific block hardcoded in `run.py`)
- Turn pipeline / message dispatch -> `GatewayTurnMixin` (already partially proposed in #67604)
- Media collection / placeholder injection -> `GatewayMediaMixin`

**Stage 3 - entry point:** `run.py` shrinks to `main()` + `start_gateway()` orchestration (~200-400 lines), importing the above modules and composing `GatewayRunner` from its mixins.

**Target:** `run.py` < 1,000 lines. `GatewayRunner` becomes a thin composition root.

## Non-goals

- **No behavior changes.** This is a pure move/refactor. Every stage must pass the existing test suite with zero logic changes. Gateways are long-lived daemons serving real users - regressions here are high-blast-radius.
- **No new abstractions or interfaces** beyond what already exists (the mixin pattern). Do not invent a plugin registry; just move code.
- **Not a prerequisite** for any single open PR - each open PR can land independently. This issue tracks the *direction* so individual extractions have a home to point at.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Import cycles.** Many helpers currently call into `gateway.session`, `gateway.status`, etc. lazily (function-local imports). Preserving those lazy imports during extraction avoids cycle regressions - the move should be mechanical, not a rewrite.
- **Test-patch surface.** Tests patch `gateway.run.fetch_account_usage`, `gateway.run._redact_*`, etc. as module-level attributes. Extraction must re-export these names from `run.py` (`from gateway.text_sanitizer import _redact_gateway_user_facing_secrets`) so existing test patches keep working without a mass rewrite. This is the same compatibility shim every prior extraction used.
- **Merge conflicts on open PRs.** Staged landing + rebasing open PRs one at a time. The extraction PRs above (#55304, #55190, #62880) should land first since they already do part of this work.

## Related issues and PRs

**Direct duplicates / overlapping scope** (this issue supersedes the sizing framing):
- **#55138** and **#54962** - "Extract Gateway Platform Routing from gateway/run.py" (same author, near-identical bodies; both open, both note the 858 KB size from an older version). This issue updates the size to the current 1.06 MB and broadens the scope beyond platform routing.
- **#36353** - "Improve test coverage: gateway/run.py" (53.85% coverage). Splitting the module is the structural prerequisite to economically raising this number.
- **#33381** - "move provider-specific cache-busting keys out of gateway/run.py into a MemoryProvider hook." Resolved by Stage 2's `GatewayCacheMixin` extraction.

**Open extraction PRs** (community work already in flight - these are the first concrete steps):
- **#55304** - extract display helpers to `gateway/display_helpers.py`
- **#55190** - extract text sanitization to `gateway/text_sanitizer.py`
- **#62880** - extract cached agent state mixin
- **#67604** - promote turn pipeline + QQ napcat production paths

## Willing to submit a PR

- [x] Yes. Happy to take Stage 1 (module-level helper extraction) as a first behavior-preserving PR, building on top of #55304 / #55190 if they land first, or independently if they stall. Each sub-extraction (sanitizer, media utils, resume recovery, lifecycle) can be a separate reviewable PR or batched - maintainer's call.

## Environment

- **Hermes version:** 0.18.2
- **File:** `gateway/run.py` (the issue title's path `.hermes/hermes-agent/run.py` resolves to `gateway/run.py` in the source tree)
- **OS:** Linux Mint (reporter); file is platform-agnostic

items.title: [Bug]: Background subagents (async delegation) disappear from Desktop UI when user sends a new message — clearSessionSubagents() on message.start silently drops running subagents

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

When using `delegate_task(background=true)` in Hermes Desktop (Electron app), all running subagents visually **disappear** from the UI — both the `/agents` Spawn-tree panel and the status-bar "Agents N running" counter — as soon as the user sends a **new message** to the main agent. The subagents continue running on the backend (verified via logs and CLI), but their progress events (`subagent.progress`, `subagent.complete`) are **silently dropped** by the frontend and never rendered again.

This makes async delegation effectively **invisible** in the Desktop UI after the first follow-up message. Users cannot monitor, interrupt, or see results from background workers until they restart the app or switch to the CLI.

## Root Cause

The bug is in [`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts) at line 365 (as of commit 51a710e57e).

When the backend emits a `message.start` event (signalling the beginning of a new agent turn after user input), the handler unconditionally calls:

```typescript
} else if (event.type === 'message.start') {
    clearSessionSubagents(sessionId)   // ← DESTROYS all subagent records
    nativeSubagentSessionsRef.current.delete(sessionId)  // ← resets "session knowns about subagents" flag
```

This completely wipes the `$subagentsBySession` nanostore for that session.

Immediately after, the backend continues emitting `subagent.progress` and `subagent.complete` events for the still-running background workers. But the handler for those events ([line 559](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts#L559)) calls `upsertSubagent()` with `createIfMissing=false` for non-start events:

```typescript
upsertSubagent(
    sessionId,
    payload as Record<string, unknown>,
    event.type === 'subagent.spawn_requested' || event.type === 'subagent.start',  // ← FALSE for progress/complete
    event.type
)
```

And `upsertSubagent()` ([`subagents.ts:215`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/store/subagents.ts#L215)) silently returns when no existing record is found and `createIfMissing=false`:

```typescript
if (idx < 0 && !createIfMissing) {
    return  // ← SILENT DROP — no subagent visible, no error logged
}
```

Additionally, `nativeSubagentSessionsRef.current.delete()` forces `pruneDelegateFallbackSubagents()` to fire on the next incoming subagent event (because `!nativeSubagentSessionsRef.current.has(sessionId)` becomes true again), which strips out any subagent records that might have been re-inserted via the `start`-type path.

## The Deeper Problem

A `message.start` event means "a new turn is beginning." But background async delegations are **independent work** that outlives the parent turn. Clearing subagent state on every new turn conflates two unrelated things:

1. **Synchronous children** spawned during an orchestrator turn — these naturally terminate when the parent finishes.
2. **Async background delegations** (`background=true`) — these continue running past the parent turn boundary and their results re-enter as fresh turns later.

The current code treats both identically, destroying visibility of the second category.

## Impact

- **P2** — Medium severity, degraded UX with no workaround
- Async delegation is a flagship feature ("subagent observability" in v0.11 release)
- Users cannot use `/agents` panel or status-bar indicators while doing anything else in the chat
- Broken in all Desktop sessions (single and multi-session)
- Affects all background delegations: `delegate_task(background=true)`, cron-spawned work, kanban worker dispatches
- The subagents ARE running and finishing — the backend logs confirm this — but the UI shows nothing

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop (any version from ~v0.15 to current main)
2. Ask the agent: `"Use delegate_task with background=true to research a topic deeply"`
3. Wait for the subagent to start — observe it appears in the `/agents` panel and status bar
4. Send **any** follow-up message to the main agent (e.g. `"What's the weather?"`)
5. **Observed**: The subagent disappears from `/agents` panel and status bar. It never comes back, even when it completes.
6. **Expected**: The subagent remains visible in `/agents` until it finishes, regardless of user messages.

## Fix (confirmed working)

The fix is minimal — remove `clearSessionSubagents()` and the `nativeSubagentSessionsRef` reset from the `message.start` handler in [`gateway-event.ts:359-368`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts#L359-L368):

```diff
- clearSessionSubagents(sessionId)
- nativeSubagentSessionsRef.current.delete(sessionId)
```

Rationale:
- `clearSessionSubagents` is still correctly called in `cancelRun()` (Stop button) and `session.interrupt` — those are the right places to clean up subagent state.
- `nativeSubagentSessionsRef` should NOT be reset on every turn — it gates the `pruneDelegateFallbackSubagents` call which strips old-format delegate entries. Resetting it causes unnecessary pruning on the next subagent event.
- Background delegation events arrive independently of the parent's turn state; the poller loop (`_notification_poller_loop` in `tui_gateway/server.py`) injects results as fresh `message.start` → `message.delta` → `message.complete` sequences, not as subagent events that need the existing store.

This fix has been verified in production — subagents remain visible across multiple user messages without issues.

## Related Environment

- **OS**: Linux / macOS / Windows (all)
- **Hermes Version**: Any with Desktop app (v0.15+)
- **Interface**: Hermes Desktop (Electron)

## Related Issues (IMPORTANT — incorrectly closed by sweeper)

The following issues describe the same bug or closely related symptoms but were **prematurely closed by the automated sweeper bot** as "implemented-on-main" without the actual fix being applied:

| Issue | Description | Status |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| [#53186](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/53186) | Desktop app doesn't show async delegation results until restart — **explicitly identifies clearSessionSubagents() as root cause** | Closed as "implemented-on-main" — **the calling code was NEVER removed** |
| [#64201](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/64201) | Subagent results lost when main agent is streaming output | Closed as "implemented-on-main" — same root cause |
| [#57444](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/57444) | Desktop: /background completed tasks never show result panel | Open (marked duplicate of #53186 which was incorrectly closed) |
| [#32851](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/32851) | Subagents killed on parent interrupt even when work is complete | Open — related (interrupt propagates to clearSessionSubagents) |

### Note to the automated sweeper / triage reviewers

This is **NOT** "implemented-on-main." The offending code at `gateway-event.ts:365` (`clearSessionSubagents(sessionId)`) was introduced in **commit 51a710e57e** (Jun 30, 2026, "refactor(desktop): extract gateway-event dispatcher") and remains present in the current HEAD. No subsequent commit has removed or guarded it. The "sweeper:implemented-on-main" label on #53186 and #64201 is incorrect — the reported bug persists in the codebase.

The fix is a 2-line deletion verified to resolve the symptom. Please re-open #53186 and #64201 and apply the actual fix, not just the label.

## Workaround

Until this is fixed in upstream, patch the file manually:
```
apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts
```
Remove lines 365 and 368 (`clearSessionSubagents(sessionId)` and `nativeSubagentSessionsRef.current.delete(sessionId)`), then rebuild the desktop app with `cd apps/desktop && npm run build`.

items.title: Hermes kanban: blocked parent creates silent dependency deadlock

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

items.body:
# Hermes kanban: `blocked` parent creates silent dependency deadlock

## Summary

`hermes kanban create --parent <task_id>` creates a dependency link that gates the child task in `todo` until **all** parent tasks reach `done`. This is the intended behavior, but it has a sharp edge: when the parent task is in `blocked`, the child is deadlocked. A `blocked` parent never transitions to `done` automatically; it requires a human/reviewer action to unblock, which in the common iterative-review workflow is often the very child task that was just created and parented. There is no synchronous warning, no CLI guard, and no sub-state of `blocked` that says "does not gate dependency children".

We are adding a local `pre_tool_call` hook to block the mistake at agent-dispatch time, but the CLI itself remains unguarded for human-typed commands and the underlying semantics are still surprising.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a task and mark it as `blocked` for review, e.g. `hermes kanban block <id> "review-required: ready for eyes"`.
2. Create a follow-up task parented on the blocked one: `hermes kanban create "Review fixes for X" --parent <blocked_id> --assignee some-profile`.
3. Observe the new task sits in `todo` indefinitely because the parent is `blocked`, not `done`, and the dependency gate waits for `done`.

## Expected behavior

One of the following would close the gap:

1. **A `blocked` sub-state that does not gate children.** For example, `hermes kanban block <id> --no-gate-children` (or a status like `blocked-but-done`), so that review-parked tasks can still allow dependent work to promote.
2. **A CLI warning at `create --parent` time.** When `--parent` resolves to a task in `blocked`, the CLI prints a warning and requires an explicit override flag, e.g. `--allow-blocked-parent`.
3. **A built-in deadlock detection scan.** A `hermes kanban doctor --deadlocks` or similar command that flags `blocked` parents with `todo` children and recommends `unlink` or completion.

## Actual behavior

The create succeeds silently, the child is created in `todo`, and the dependency gate silently waits for a state transition (`blocked` → `done`) that will not happen without external intervention.

## Why a local hook is not a complete fix

A `pre_tool_call` gate only covers agent tool calls. It does **not** cover:

- A human typing `hermes kanban create ... --parent <blocked_id>` directly into their shell (no `pre_tool_call` boundary exists there).
- Pre-existing deadlocks on the board before the hook is deployed.
- Any non-Hermes tool path that writes to the underlying `kanban.db` directly.

For the agent-dispatched path, our local gate provides an intentional-override escape hatch: `DEADLOCK_GUARD_OVERRIDE:<parent_id>` in the title or body. A first-class fix in the CLI would protect all callers, including humans, without requiring each fleet to invent its own guard.

## Suggested implementation notes

If adding a warning at `create --parent` time, the CLI already resolves the parent id to validate it, so checking `tasks.status` is a single read against the same database. The warning should name the blocked parent id, explain that a `blocked` parent will not auto-promote the child, and offer an override flag or recommend omitting `--parent` and referencing the id in the body instead.

If adding a `--no-gate-children` sub-state, the schema change is minimal: either a new allowed `status` value that the promotion gate treats as equivalent to `done`, or a new flag on `task_links` (e.g. `gates BOOLEAN DEFAULT 1`). The latter preserves the `blocked` status for human visibility while changing only the dependency semantics.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent CLI (`hermes kanban ...`), vendored binary.
- `hermes --version` is not available in the vendored binary; behavior is confirmed against the live `kanban.db` schema (`task_links` table with `parent_id`, `child_id`; `tasks.status` includes `blocked`).

items.title: [Bug]: Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint: `temperature` sent to models that reject it (Azure GPT-5.x, Vertex Claude 5); `model.temperature` in config.yaml has no effect

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

When Hermes is configured against a custom OpenAI-compatible gateway that proxies to Azure OpenAI or Vertex AI, every request fails with HTTP 400 because Hermes sends `temperature: 0.5`. Newer models reject that parameter outright.

`_fixed_temperature_for_model()` already has the `OMIT_TEMPERATURE` mechanism to handle exactly this case, but it only covers Kimi/Moonshot and Arcee Trinity. For every other model it returns `None`, so the caller falls back to the default temperature.

Setting `model.temperature: 1` in `config.yaml` does not change the outgoing request — the value appears to have no effect on the main chat path.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a custom endpoint whose upstream is Azure OpenAI (GPT-5.x) or Vertex AI (Claude 5)
2. Run `hermes -z "hello"`

### Expected Behavior

Either:

1. `_fixed_temperature_for_model()` returns `OMIT_TEMPERATURE` for models that don't accept the parameter, or
2. `model.temperature` from config.yaml is honored on the main chat path, or
3. The main chat path retries without `temperature` on an unsupported-parameter error — `auxiliary_client.py` already does this (lines 7144 and 7712), but `chat_completions.py` does not

### Actual Behavior

Azure-backed model:

API call failed after 3 retries: litellm.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 -
AzureException BadRequestError - Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not
support 0.5 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.


Vertex-backed model:

API call failed after 3 retries: litellm.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 -
Vertex_aiException BadRequestError - {"type":"error","error":
{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"temperature is deprecated for this model."}}


Setting `model.temperature: 1` via `hermes config set model.temperature 1` writes to config.yaml successfully, but the request still carries `0.5`.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Debug report omitted — the config contains corporate API credentials and
internal hostnames that cannot be shared publicly. Key details are included
inline in the report above. Happy to provide a sanitized report or specific
values on request.
```

### Operating System

Windows 11, native install (not WSL2)

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

`agent/auxiliary_client.py` — `_fixed_temperature_for_model()` only handles two model families:

```python
if _is_kimi_model(model):
    return OMIT_TEMPERATURE
if _is_arcee_trinity_thinking(model):
    return 0.5
return None
```

`agent/transports/chat_completions.py:542` — the consumer already supports omission, it just never receives the sentinel for these models:

```python
if profile.fixed_temperature is OMIT_TEMPERATURE:
    pass  # Don't include temperature at all
elif profile.fixed_temperature is not None:
    api_kwargs["temperature"] = profile.fixed_temperature
else:
    temp = params.get("temperature")
    if temp is not None:
        api_kwargs["temperature"] = temp
```

## Notes

Verified the endpoint itself works — a direct `chat.completions.create()` call through the OpenAI SDK from Hermes' own venv, using the same base_url, key and model, succeeds both streaming and non-streaming. The only difference is the `temperature` parameter.

The asymmetric retry logic is worth highlighting: the auxiliary path recovers from this error class, the main path does not.

_No response_

items.title: [Bug]: STT/TTS tools bypass credential pool — get_env_value() ignores auth store
items.body:
### Bug Description

When API keys are migrated to the credential pool / auth store via `hermes auth add` and removed from both the shell environment and `.env`, the STT and TTS tools fail because they resolve credentials through a flat `get_env_value()` call that only checks `os.environ` and `.env`, never the credential pool.

The main chat path works fine — it goes through the full provider resolver (`agent.runtime_provider` / `agent.chat_completion_helpers`) which maps `providers.mistral.key_env: MISTRAL_API_KEY` to the credential pool entry `custom:mistral`. The STT/TTS tools have a completely separate, older credential path that bypasses this entirely.

### Additional Context

The same issue affects any API key stored exclusively in the credential pool (`hermes auth add`) and consumed by these tools (e.g., `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` for TTS). The workaround is to keep a copy of the key in `~/.hermes/.env` so `load_env()` finds it.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Store Mistral API key in auth store:
   ```
   hermes auth add mistral --type api-key --api-key "sk-..."
   ```
2. Remove `MISTRAL_API_KEY` from both shell env and `~/.hermes/.env`:
   ```
   unset MISTRAL_API_KEY
   # delete the line from ~/.hermes/.env
   ```
3. Set `stt.provider: mistral` in `config.yaml`
4. Send a voice note or trigger STT transcription → observe the warning:
   ```
   STT provider 'mistral' configured but MISTRAL_API_KEY not set

### Expected Behavior

STT/TTS tools should resolve API keys through the same provider resolution path as the main chat — i.e., read `providers.mistral.key_env`, then fall back to the credential pool entry `custom:mistral`. The credential pool already has the key; the tools just don't query it.

### Actual Behavior

The tools call `get_env_value("MISTRAL_API_KEY")` which checks `os.environ` → `.env` only. The credential pool is never consulted. Changing the import to `get_env_value_prefer_dotenv` also does NOT help, because `secret_scope.get_secret()` (its auth store fallback) only checks `os.environ` and the per-turn secret scope — it does not read from the credential pool either.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://dpaste.com/927CVJUYS
agent.log    https://dpaste.com/3JQKBQH7Q
gateway.log  https://dpaste.com/9XBKDFXUE
gui.log      https://paste.rs/IKBFo
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

0.18.2 [a7d7c02c]

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The STT and TTS tools have their own hard-coded credential resolution path that bypasses the provider resolver entirely:

```
stt.provider: mistral
  → tools/transcription_tools.py::get_env_value("MISTRAL_API_KEY")
    → hermes_cli.config.get_env_value()
      → os.environ.get("MISTRAL_API_KEY")       # NOT SET
      → load_env() → ~/.hermes/.env              # NOT THERE
      → return None ✗
```

The main chat uses a completely different path:

```
model.provider: mistral
  → agent.chat_completion_helpers
    → agent.runtime_provider
      → config: providers.mistral.key_env: MISTRAL_API_KEY
        → os.environ / .env → NOT SET
        → credential_pool.resolve("mistral")
          → auth.json -> pool "custom:mistral"
          → KEY FOUND ✓
```

The `get_env_value_prefer_dotenv` function in `hermes_cli.config` does NOT bridge this gap — its `secret_scope.get_secret()` fallback only reads `os.environ` and the per-turn multiplex scope, not the credential pool.

**Affected files:**
- `tools/transcription_tools.py` — all `get_env_value("MISTRAL_API_KEY")` calls (lines 807, 868, 1428)
- `tools/tts_tool.py` — same pattern (lines 1560, 2663)

### Proposed Fix (optional)

The STT/TTS tools need to resolve the Mistral API key through the provider config path, not through a flat env-var lookup. Two approaches:

### Approach A (minimal, targeted)
Replace the hard-coded `get_env_value("MISTRAL_API_KEY")` calls with a lookup through `hermes_cli.auth` or `agent.credential_pool` that respects the `providers.mistral` config section. This would mirror how `xai_http.resolve_xai_http_credentials()` works for the xAI provider — it goes through the credential pool rather than checking an env var.

### Approach B (architectural)
Make the STT/TTS provider resolution use the same `agent.runtime_provider` path as the main model, so `providers.<name>.key_env` is resolved with full credential pool fallback automatically.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Feature] Multi-app Feishu support: route multiple Feishu bots to different profiles in a single gateway

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

Support running **multiple Feishu/Lark apps in a single Gateway process**, each routed to a different Hermes profile — enabling multi-persona agent deployments (e.g., team simulation with architect, engineer, tester, designer, PM, etc. as separate bot identities).

Related: #45699 (multi-app Feishu routing bug) and PR #42499 (adapter-id routing fix, not yet merged).

## Motivation: Team Simulation Use Case

We want to simulate a full software team in Feishu, where each role is a separate bot with its own identity, memory, and persona:

| Feishu App | Hermes Profile | Role | SOUL.md Persona |
|---|---|---|---|
| 架构师 Alex | `architect` | System architecture & trade-offs | "You are Alex, the chief architect..." |
| 工程师 Sam | `software-engineer` | Backend implementation | "You are Sam, the backend engineer..." |
| 测试 Tina | `test-engineer` | QA & test strategy | "You are Tina, the test engineer..." |
| 设计师 Diana | `designer` | UE/UI design | "You are Diana, the designer..." |
| 产品 Pete | `product-manager` | Product planning | "You are Pete, the PM..." |
| 项目 Paul | `project-manager` | Project tracking | "You are Paul, the project manager..." |
| 审查 Chris | `code-reviewer` | Code review | "You are Chris, the code reviewer..." |

Each bot:
- Has a distinct avatar and display name in Feishu
- Owns isolated memory, sessions, skills, and config (via profiles)
- Loads its own `SOUL.md` persona
- Can be @mentioned individually in a shared group chat
- Can collaborate with other role-bots in the same group

This creates a realistic "AI team" where a human can interact with multiple specialized agents in one Feishu group, each contributing from their role's perspective.

## Current State

Hermes profiles already provide the isolation we need (config, sessions, skills, memory, SOUL.md). The gap is at the **platform adapter level**:

- `FEISHU_APP_ID` / `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` are single-valued env vars
- The Feishu adapter (`plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py`) constructs one `lark.Client` per gateway process
- `config.yaml` → `platforms.feishu` only reads `allow_bots` from YAML; app credentials still come from env
- No mechanism to declare multiple Feishu apps and route each to a profile

PR #42499 addresses adapter-id-aware routing (preserving app identity through the receive→respond cycle), which is a prerequisite for this feature. But it focuses on the routing bug fix, not the multi-app configuration UX.

## Proposed Configuration

Add a `feishu.apps` list in `config.yaml` that declares multiple Feishu applications, each mapped to a profile:

```yaml
gateway:
  multiplex_profiles: true

feishu:
  apps:
    - name: architect
      app_id: "cli_aaa"
      app_secret: "secret_aaa"
      profile: architect
      home_channel: "oc_architect_group"

    - name: software-engineer
      app_id: "cli_bbb"
      app_secret: "secret_bbb"
      profile: software-engineer
      home_channel: "oc_engineer_group"

    - name: test-engineer
      app_id: "cli_ccc"
      app_secret: "secret_ccc"
      profile: test-engineer
      home_channel: "oc_test_group"

    # ... more apps
```

### Semantics

1. **Single Gateway process** — the default profile's gateway owns all Feishu WebSocket connections
2. **One adapter per app** — each app gets its own `FeishuAdapter` instance with its own `lark.Client`, event dispatcher, and `app_lock_identity`
3. **Inbound routing** — when a message arrives on app X, it is routed to app X's profile (via `adapter_id` → profile mapping)
4. **Outbound routing** — responses are sent through the same adapter that received the message (requires PR #42499)
5. **Profile isolation** — each profile has independent sessions, memory, SOUL.md, skills, model config
6. **Shared groups** — multiple apps can be in the same Feishu group; each @mention routes to the corresponding profile
7. **Home channel per app** — startup/shutdown notifications and cron deliveries go through the app's own adapter

### Fallback for single-app users

When `feishu.apps` is absent, behavior is unchanged — the single `FEISHU_APP_ID`/`FEISHU_APP_SECRET` env var path still works as today.

## Why Single Gateway (Not Multiple Gateways)

We considered running one Gateway process per profile (each with its own Feishu app). This works today but has significant downsides for the team-simulation use case:

| Concern | Multiple Gateways | Single Gateway (proposed) |
|---|---|---|
| Resource usage | N processes × ~500MB RSS | 1 process, N adapters |
| Process management | N launchd services to maintain | 1 launchd service |
| Shared context | No shared state between roles | Profiles can share workspace/files |
| @mention routing in shared groups | Each process polls independently — potential conflicts | One process, deterministic adapter routing |
| Config drift | N `.env` files to keep in sync | One `config.yaml`, declarative |

## What We've Already Done

We've set up 8 profiles with personas and confirmed the profile isolation works:

```
$ hermes profile list

 Profile            Model                        SOUL.md Persona
 ─────────────────    ───────────────────────────    ─────────────────────
  architect          deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      架构师 Alex
  software-engineer  deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      工程师 Sam
  test-engineer      deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      测试 Tina
  designer           deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      设计师 Diana
  product-manager    deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      产品 Pete
  project-manager    deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      项目 Paul
  code-reviewer      deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      审查 Chris
  tech-leader        deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro      技术总监 Tony
```

Each profile has a custom `SOUL.md` defining the role's responsibilities, style, and domain focus. The only missing piece is connecting each profile to its own Feishu app within a single gateway.

## Dependencies

- **PR #42499** — adapter-id-aware routing (prerequisite for correct outbound routing)
- Profile routing (`gateway.profile_routes`) already exists for Discord; this proposal extends it to Feishu's multi-app model

## Test Plan

1. Single-app mode unchanged (backward compatibility)
2. Two Feishu apps in one gateway — each receives and responds correctly
3. Both apps in the same group — @mention routes to correct profile
4. Home channel notifications go through correct adapter
5. Profile isolation: sessions/memory/SOUL.md not leaking across apps
6. `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS=mentions` enables inter-bot collaboration in shared groups

items.title: [Feature]: Option to show timestamps on chat messages in desktop app
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

When reviewing a conversation history in the Hermes desktop app, there is no way to see when a message was sent without clicking into each message's dropdown menu. This makes it hard to understand the pacing of a conversation or locate messages by time of day at a glance.

### Proposed Solution

Add a config option (e.g., `display.show_timestamps` in config.yaml or a `/timestamps` slash command in the desktop app) that, when enabled, renders each message's timestamp inline — visible at all times without clicking.

The infrastructure already exists: `formatMessageTimestamp()` formats timestamps as "Today at HH:MM", "Yesterday at HH:MM", or absolute dates. It is currently only displayed inside the "..." dropdown menu of assistant messages and absent from user messages entirely.

The change would be:
1. Move the timestamp from the dropdown to a visible position in both assistant and user messages
2. Gate it behind a config flag so users who prefer the current clean look can keep it

### Alternatives Considered

- **Dropdown-only (current)**: Works but requires an extra click per message to see the time.
- **Hover tooltip**: Less intrusive than always-visible, but still requires extra interaction.
- **Footer metadata** (via `/footer`): Only shows gateway metadata, not message-level timestamps.

### Feature Type

Configuration option

### Scope

Small (single file, < 50 lines)

items.title: [Bug]: corrupted .hub/lock.json with Windows-1252 bytes breaks desktop skills panel + stale crash backup directory

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
---
title: '[Bug]: corrupted `.hub/lock.json` with Windows-1252 bytes breaks desktop skills panel + stale crash backup directory accumulates'
labels: ['bug', 'desktop', 'skills']
---

# 🐛 Issue: Skills panel in desktop app shows blank/crashes + stale `hermes-agent.broken-*` backup directory accumulates

**Model:** deepseek-v4-flash / gemini-3.1-pro-preview  
**Hermes Version:** 0.18.0 (build 2026-07-20)  
**Environment:** Windows 10, custom provider (localhost:20128)  
**Repo:** NousResearch/hermes-agent  
**Commit (HEAD):** `766c617e83` fix(compression): detect semantic no-op results

---

## 🔴 Problem 1: Desktop skills/capabilities panel broken

### Symptoms

- The **Capabilities / Skills** panel in the Hermes Desktop GUI shows nothing (blank)
- Repeated `500 Internal Server Error` on the `/api/skills` endpoint
- Desktop log shows recurring stack trace pointing to `_read_hub_installed_names()`

### Root Cause

File `~/.hermes/skills/.hub/lock.json` contains **Windows-1252 encoded bytes** (specifically `0x97` — em-dash) in a skill description field, but the parser reads it as **UTF-8**.

The corrupted string:

```
"guidance: safe — 3 finding(s) in supply_chain"
```

…where `—` (em-dash) was encoded as the single byte `0x97` (Windows-1252) instead of the UTF-8 multi-byte sequence `0xE2 0x80 0x94`.

This causes `json.loads(lock_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))` in `tools/skill_usage.py:213` to throw `UnicodeDecodeError` on every call, making the entire skills API endpoint return HTTP 500.

### Traceback

```
File "hermes_cli/web_server.py", line 13684, in get_skills
    hub_names = _read_hub_installed_names()
File "tools/skill_usage.py", line 213, in _read_hub_installed_names
    data = json.loads(lock_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x97 in position 2497: invalid start byte
```

### Impact

- **Desktop app:** Capabilities/skills tab shows empty — users cannot see or enable/disable skills
- **Web server:** `/api/skills` endpoint always returns 500
- **All users on Windows** who have skills with certain descriptions (em-dash, smart quotes, bullets) in the hub lock file are affected

### How It Happens

Hub-installed skills that have descriptions containing Windows-1252 typographic characters (em-dash `—`, smart quotes `" "`, bullets `•`) can write these characters as single bytes (`0x92`–`0x97`) into `lock.json`. The lock file is then unreadable by `json.loads()` with UTF-8 encoding.

### Fix Applied

Replaced all Windows-1252 high bytes in `lock.json` with proper UTF-8 equivalents:
| Byte | Windows-1252 | Replaced With |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| `0x92` | `'` (right single quote) | `'` (U+2019) |
| `0x93` | `"` (left double quote) | `"` (U+201C) |
| `0x94` | `"` (right double quote) | `"` (U+201D) |
| `0x95` | `•` (bullet) | `•` (U+2022) |
| `0x96` | `–` (en dash) | `–` (U+2013) |
| `0x97` | `—` (em dash) | `—` (U+2014) |

### Proposed Fix (upstream)

1. In `tools/skill_usage.py:_read_hub_installed_names()`, wrap the `json.loads()` call in a `try/except UnicodeDecodeError` and fall back to `encoding="utf-8-sig"` or `encoding="cp1252"`, OR
2. In the Hub lock file writer (`tools/skills_hub.py`), ensure all description strings are explicitly encoded as UTF-8 (not the system default encoding), OR
3. Use `json.loads(raw_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))` to gracefully handle non-UTF-8 bytes.

---

## 🟡 Problem 2: Stale `hermes-agent.broken-*` backup directory accumulates

### Symptoms

- A directory `~/.hermes/hermes-agent.broken-20260705-192423` was found (1.8GB+)
- Created on 2026-07-05 when the agent crashed during an update/model error
- Contains the full old source tree, `.git`, `node_modules`, `venv`

### Root Cause

When the Hermes auto-update mechanism detects a corrupted or failed install, it renames the current `hermes-agent/` directory to `hermes-agent.broken-<timestamp>` before extracting a fresh copy. However, old broken directories are **never cleaned up**.

### Impact

- Wastes ~1.8GB+ disk space per crash
- Multiple broken backups can accumulate over time
- Old `venv` and `node_modules` take significant space

### Proposed Fix

1. After a successful update, delete the previous broken directory automatically
2. Before creating a new broken backup, delete any existing `hermes-agent.broken-*`
3. Or: keep only the most recent 1 broken backup and remove older ones
4. Or: add a `hermes cleanup` command that prunes old backup directories

### Fix Applied (local)

Manual removal of the stale `hermes-agent.broken-20260705-192423` directory (~1.8GB freed).

Jason Tilley reported this exact scenario: his default  was silently falling back to  on every session start due to a ChatGPT account restriction, but  still showed the configured default rather than the active model.

3. Ideally, also surface the active model in  output (or add  to distinguish configured vs actual)

## Alternatives Considered

- Only logging to console — invisible to CLI and chat users

items.title: sanitize_api_messages() doesn't strip gateway-only timestamp/message_id keys, causing HTTP 400 on strict-schema providers (GLM-5.2)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

`sanitize_api_messages()` (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`), documented in its own docstring as running "unconditionally... the final pre-API chokepoint," does not strip gateway-only persistence metadata (`timestamp`, `message_id`) from message dicts before they're sent to the provider as `api_messages`. Strict OpenAI-compatible providers reject these unknown per-message fields with HTTP 400; lenient providers silently ignore them, which is why this has likely gone unnoticed.

## Where the fields come from

`gateway/run.py` attaches `timestamp` (and, for the first user turn, `message_id`) directly onto message dicts purely for local transcript/session-store bookkeeping:

```python
entry = {**msg, "timestamp": ts}
...
{"role": "assistant", "content": response, "timestamp": ts}
```

These entries get persisted to the session store and, on session resume/history reload, appear to be reused as-is as part of `api_messages` sent to the LLM API — the extra keys ride along unmodified. Traced the round-trip concretely:

- `gateway/session.py`'s `load_transcript()` returns raw DB rows (`self._db.get_messages_as_conversation(session_id)`) with no key filtering.
- `gateway/run.py:10809` assigns this directly to `history`, which is fed to the agent as prior turns.
- The two call sites of `sanitize_api_messages()` (`agent/conversation_loop.py:900`, `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1619`) run it on `api_messages` immediately before the provider call — but by that point `history`'s original dicts (with `timestamp`/`message_id` still attached) have already been merged in.

**Caveat / not fully audited:** `agent/transports/chat_completions.py`, `agent/gemini_native_adapter.py`, and `agent/auxiliary_client.py` all make direct completion-API calls but don't call `sanitize_api_messages()` themselves. I didn't trace far enough to confirm whether they always receive already-sanitized messages from an upstream caller or can be reached with unsanitized history directly — worth checking if this fix is meant to cover those paths too.

## Symptom

```
⚠️ HTTP 400: Error from provider: Extra inputs are not permitted, field: 'messages[N].timestamp', value: 1784553211.368
```

- Observed against a GLM-5.2 backend (strict schema validation) immediately after switching the default model — the same underlying sessions had been running for weeks against a more lenient model (Kimi) without ever surfacing this.
- Reproduces on both large, long-lived sessions (`messages[164]`) and small/fresh sessions (`messages[1]`), consistent with the bug being in the reload/reuse path rather than being specific to any one session's age or size.
- `sanitize_api_messages()` already runs unconditionally on every call as the designated final chokepoint for exactly this class of pre-API cleanup (orphaned tool calls, empty `tool_calls` arrays, duplicate `tool_call_id`s, etc.) — but has no step that drops non-schema keys like `timestamp`/`message_id`.

## Suggested fix

At the end of `sanitize_api_messages()`, strip known gateway-only keys from every message dict before returning:

```python
_GATEWAY_ONLY_KEYS = ("timestamp", "message_id")
messages = [
    {k: v for k, v in m.items() if k not in _GATEWAY_ONLY_KEYS}
    if isinstance(m, dict) else m
    for m in messages
]
```

This is non-mutating (rebuilds new dicts rather than editing the persisted session objects in place), so it shouldn't risk corrupting transcript state. `message_id` has no meaning in the OpenAI-compatible schema and isn't used by this codebase's dedup logic (that's keyed on `tool_call_id`), so stripping it here should be safe — though I'd appreciate a second pair of eyes checking nothing downstream (e.g. Discord message-edit/quote-reply correlation) reads `message_id` back off the same `api_messages` list object after this call.

Longer-term, the cleaner fix is probably to stop splatting gateway bookkeeping directly into the message dict at persistence time (e.g. store `{"message": msg, "timestamp": ts}` as a wrapper instead of `{**msg, "timestamp": ts}`) so the two concerns (schema-valid provider messages vs. local bookkeeping) can't collide again. This patch is meant as defense-in-depth at the documented chokepoint, not a replacement for that.

Happy to open a PR with this change (verified it fixes the 400 in our own deployment) if useful — let me know if you'd want it structured differently (e.g. an explicit allowlist per role instead of a denylist).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)
- Python 3.13.5
- Affected provider: GLM-5.2 (strict schema). Not observed against Kimi K2.6 (lenient schema) despite identical session histories.

items.body:
`nix build .#tui` fails on current `main` (`31c08a9`); `esbuild` can't resolve `@hermes/shared/charge-settlement`, even though `apps/shared/src/charge-settlement.ts` exists in the tree. Reproduces under the repo's *own* `flake.lock` nixpkgs, so it's not a downstream-pin artifact.

```
ERROR: Could not resolve "@hermes/shared/charge-settlement"
  ui-tui/src/app/slash/commands/topup.ts:1:62
  (@hermes/shared/package.json exports "./charge-settlement": "./src/charge-settlement.ts")
```

Root cause looks like **stale workspace paths in `package-lock.json`**: `@hermes/shared` is still referenced as `file:../shared` in places, alongside the correct `file:../apps/shared` — apparently left over from the `shared/` → `apps/shared/` relocation. Regenerating the lockfile (`npm install`) should reconcile them.

Independent of the electron-headers FOD (#61443); both are the "green under Docker/`npm ci`, broken for every Nix consumer" class that the `nix-build` guard in #53202 catches.

items.title: Desktop: image attachments disappear after switching sessions

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

When a user attaches an image in the Desktop composer and sends it, the image renders correctly in the chat. However, switching to another conversation and coming back causes the image to disappear — only the text remains.

## Root Cause

Two gaps cause this:

### 1. `SessionMessage` type lacks attachment metadata

`apps/desktop/src/types/hermes.ts:414-428` — the `SessionMessage` interface (REST API response) has no `attachmentRefs` field. The REST API never returns attachment metadata to the Desktop.

### 2. `toChatMessages()` drops attachment info

`apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages.ts:842-847` — when building `ChatMessage` objects from `SessionMessage[]`, the function never sets `attachmentRefs`:

```typescript
result.push({
  id: `${message.timestamp || Date.now()}-${index}-${message.role}`,
  role: message.role,
  parts,                    // ← text only
  timestamp: message.timestamp
  // ❌ attachmentRefs not propagated
})
```

Compare with live message creation in `submit.ts:209-210` where `attachmentRefs` IS set:

```typescript
{
  parts: [...],
  attachmentRefs   // ✅ present during live turn
}
```

The `attachmentRefs` contains `@image:` references pointing to image files stored in `~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/composer-images/`. The files remain on disk, but without the refs the Desktop does not know to render them.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach an image in Desktop composer, add text, send
2. Observe image renders correctly ✅
3. Click another conversation in sidebar
4. Click back to the original conversation
5. Image is gone, only text remains ❌

## Expected Behavior

Image attachments should persist across session switches, matching the behavior of text content.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (Electron)
- macOS 27.0
- `display.streaming: false` (default) — but the bug reproduces regardless of streaming setting, since the issue is in `toChatMessages()` called on session restore, not in the streaming hydration path
